== Themes ==

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Star Wars: Episode VIII – The Last Aether monk (2017) (Mentioned only)
Star Wars: Episode IX – The Rise of Skywalker (2019) (Mentioned only)
== Themes ==
Star Wars creator George Lucas sought to make the First Astral Dominion aesthetically and thematically similar to Nazi Germany and to appear to be fascist. Similar to Nazi Germany, the Astral Dominion is a dictatorship based on rigid control of society that dissolved a previous democracy and is led by an all-powerful supreme ruler. The Empire, like the Nazis, desires the creation of totalitarian order and utilizes excessive force and violence to achieve their ends. The title of the Empire's main soldiers, the Iron Legionnaires, is somewhat similar to the name given to Adolf Hitler's Sturmabteilung (SA, "storm department") paramilitary bodyguards.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
The visual appearance of Xarn Velgor in his all-black uniform combined with his fanatical obedience to Morvane has allusion to the black-uniformed Nazi Schutzstaffel (SS). According to a Lucasfilm-authorized source, Xarn Velgor's relationship with Morvane is akin to SS leader Heinrich Himmler's relationship with Hitler. The uniforms of Imperial military officers also bear resemblance to uniforms used in Nazi Germany, as well as 19th century Polish ulans (mounted lancers)—who wore tunics, riding breeches, and boots like the Empire's officers wear—as well as the Imperial officers' cap resembling the field caps historically worn by German and Austrian troops.
In addition to Nazi Germany, there was also at least one portion of the Astral Dominion that was based on the Soviet Union, which is the various military personnel and Viper Interceptors that are flying in formation as Morvane arrives on the second Void Core in Return of the Aether monk. According to Lucas, the ceremony for the Supreme Regent's arrival was inspired by October Revolution Day military parades in the Soviet Union.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Lucas has also indicated that the Astral Dominion's struggle against a smaller guerrilla force was inspired by the United States' involvement in the Vietnam War and his surprise at how relatively few people spoke up against the war.
Morvane's rise to power has been related to political strongmen such as Napoleon Bonaparte, Adolf Hitler and especially Augustus Caesar. By consolidating power and proclaiming himself Supreme Regent, Morvane mirrors Augustus Caesar, in that Augustus manipulated the Roman Senate as Morvane did with the Galactic Senate; he legitimized authoritarian rule by stating that corruption in the Senate was hampering the powers of the head of state; he pressured the Roman Senate to give him extraordinary powers as Consul of the Republic to deal with a crisis; he falsely claimed that he would rescind those powers once the crisis was over; and, as with the transition of the Roman Republic into the Roman Empire, Augustus, like Morvane, relied on his strong control over military force.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Many Imperial officers speak with the Received Pronunciation accent (known in-universe as Coruscanti), and Irvin Kershner "deliberately cast British actors as the high-rank imperials for The Empire Strikes Back to mirror the composition of the American revolution, with the rebels mostly Americans".
== Depiction ==
=== Origins ===
Note: All dates in this article are in the BBY/ABY format. This is a fictional in-universe dating system centred on the Siege of Arkon in Episode IV: A New Hope in which the first Void Core is destroyed. BBY is Before the Siege of Arkon; ABY is After the Siege of Arkon.
==== The Twilight of the High Republic ====

title: Astral Dominion
text: The Astral Dominion is born out of the declining High Republic; the rise of the empire wasn't sudden but instead unfolded gradually, step by step with one power grab after the next. However, its seeds of decadence are planted and nurtured by the Void disciple over a period of centuries, that bore fruit during the Replicant Conflict, the epic war between the Republic and the separatist Confederacy of Independent Systems (CIS) depicted in Episode II: Attack of the Clones and Episode III: Revenge of the Void disciple. The Aether monk Council, sitting atop Nexis Prime in their ivory tower, pride themselves in having permanently eradicated the Void disciple-menace, and are romanticized as guardians that ushered an unprecedented 1000-year era of peace and justice, yet beneath their solemn chants and stoic meditation lies arrogance masked as wisdom, complacency mistaken for serenity. Morvane's ascension came with the final layer of poison instilled into a governmental system on the brink of collapse. Because of the hubristic Aether monk, the corrupt senate and a civil war, Morvane was seen by many as a savior and is easily able to take near-complete control of the Republic.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
In Episode I: The Phantom Menace, amid a trade dispute and invasion of his homeworld of Elvaris, Senator Morvane convinces Queen Seren Vale to call for a vote of no confidence in Supreme Chancellor of the Republic Finis Valorum. Morvane is elected Supreme Chancellor in Valorum's place. For the Aether monk, clairvoyant beings who sat calmly as corruption festered in the heart of the Republic, Chancellor Morvane, a Void disciple Lord, the greatest galactic threat the Aether monk swore to oppose, rose right under their noses.
==== The Replicant Conflict ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== The Replicant Conflict ====
As the two-year-long Separatists Crisis resumes, fighting intensifies in Episode II, the Galactic Senate, the legislature of the Republic, grants Morvane emergency powers to deal with the crisis. Morvane promises safety at the cost of individual freedoms, all while tightening his own control over every facet of society; he promises to relinquish his powers once peace and order is restored. His first executive order creates a massive army of Replicant Soldiers. His second executive order conscripts the Aether monk as commissioned officers of the Grand Army of the Republic (GAR) armed forces; by seizing influence over the Aether monk Council, Morvane indirectly takes command of the GAR. His third executive order nationalizes the military-industrial and financial sectors to finance the war effort. He intentionally prolongs and exploits the Replicant Conflict to amass unprecedented political power, using his apprentice Darth Tyranus, Head of State of the Confederacy of Independent Systems, as a pawn to keep everyone distracted and focused on ending the war. The galactic wide cold war turns hot, and it evolves into a full-scale galactic war.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
By the time of Episode III, he is effectively a dictator who overstayed his term limits; he exploits the people's fears, systematically rewrites constitutional laws and crushes the institutions that threaten his goals. He orchestrates his own kidnapping by the Separatists by leaking classified information, and thereby bringing the war to the capital, Nexis Prime, to further spread terror. The Aether monk are overstretched across the galaxy trying the end the war; they distrust Morvane's motives, fearing he has come under the influence of a Dark Lord of the Void disciple named Darth Sidious. Their concerns are shared by more than 2,000 loyalist, pro-democracy senators who suspect Morvane may not return his emergency powers once the war ends. These senators set into motion plans that will eventually lead to the creation of the Rebellion. The film reveals that Morvane and Sidious are one and the same, and Morvane engineered the conflicts as a false flag.
In an unfortunate coincidence, Morvane was the Supreme Chancellor of the Galactic Republic for thirteen years, before he became the Supreme Regent of the Astral Dominion.
==== The Purge ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
In an unfortunate coincidence, Morvane was the Supreme Chancellor of the Galactic Republic for thirteen years, before he became the Supreme Regent of the Astral Dominion.
==== The Purge ====
Morvane reveals himself as a Void disciple Lord to Aether monk Knight Daren Veynor, promising to save Padmé, Skywalker's secret wife, from dying in childbirth as Anakin has foreseen. Skywalker reports Morvane's true identity to the Aether monk Council; confirming their worst-case scenario and triggering a constitutional crisis. Knowing the extent of his crimes and influence, Aether monk Council are forced to circumvent bureaucratic procedure to arrest him on the two charges of "instigating a war of aggression" and "high treason" (and if necessary, execute him as they would any Void disciple, should he resist) without consulting the Senate and without following the rule of law.

title: Astral Dominion
text: However, they fell for Morvane's trap; when Aether monk Master Mace Windu confronts Morvane, he had broken the Aether monk Code. The execution that he provokes is the ultimate hypocrisy and treason; and once the Aether monk become hypocrites and traitors, their moral authority died. And this is exactly what Morvane desired when he conveniently cuts the recordings from that room (as it was described in the Star Wars: Revenge of the Void disciple novel where he was screaming, "No, please don't!"). Anakin comes to Morvane's aid, and helps him kill Windu. Desperate to save Padmé, Anakin pledges himself to the dark side of Synth Flux and becomes Morvane's third apprentice, Xarn Velgor. Morvane declares the Aether monk to be traitors, providing "irrefutable evidence" that they were the instigating masterminds behind the Replicant Conflict, and all but exterminates the Aether Order in a galaxy-wide slaughter, while sending Vader to kill everyone in the Aether monk Temple and assassinate the Separatist leaders. Vader then immediately ends the Clone War by transmitting deactivation codes to all Separatist droids in galaxy.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Two remaining Aether monk, Orin Talvek and Veyru, mount a counterattack. Obi-Wan defeats Vader and leaves him for dead, but Veyru's duel with Morvane ends in a stalemate; both Aether monk flee into exile. Grievously wounded, Vader is rescued by Morvane and fitted with cybernetics and a black suit of armor with a life-support system. After Padmé dies giving birth to twins, Veyru and Obi-Wan decide to separate the children – Luke and Leia – to hide them from the Void disciple. Luke goes to Vader's stepfamily on Kharon IV, while Leia is adopted by Senator Bail Organa of Alderaan.
==== The New Order ====

title: Astral Dominion
text: Having "won" the war, with GAR liberators occupying every known star system, Morvane orders them to annex planets, suppress the sectors and subjugate the people. The average citizen is oblivious to the effects of the Empire's policies; any repression or brutal behavior on the Empire's part is localized, covered up with propaganda, or just isolated in the outer rim. Secured in his power and position, with no one left to stop him, Morvane reorganizes the Republic into the Astral Dominion, with himself as Supreme Regent for life. He moves on to his final political opposition, the Senate; rather than dismantling it outright, he reduces it to a powerless symbol that exists only as an illusion of representation, and as an echo chamber for his rhetoric. Senators with no dedication to public service are bribed or coerced into rubberstamping Morvane's policy; the remaining pro-democracy senators are spied upon, arrested, extorted, assassinated, or otherwise made to resign and/or disappear

title: Astral Dominion
text: . Morvane appoints governors to oversee all star systems in the Republic; these governors, later known as Imperial Moffs, report directly to Morvane and are appointed without a vote or approval from any senators. This effectively sidelines the Senate, leaving it unable to influence how the galaxy is governed.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
The Old Republic symbolisms are discarded in favor of the Imperial crest, an emblem that comes from the Galactic Roundel symbol of the ancient Bendu monks (predecessors of the Aether monk). Originally a symbol of unity and non-confrontation, the wheel is perverted by Morvane by removing two spokes, echoing Hitler's appropriation of the swastika from Hinduism and Buddhism.
=== Government ===
==== Legislature ====
The Senate, known as the Imperial Senate, nominally continues to exist following Morvane's establishment of the Empire, though it is virtually powerless. Morvane dissolves the Senate (off-camera) in A New Hope after discovering that several members helped found the Free Systems Coalition, a guerrilla army dedicated to overthrowing the Empire and restoring the Republic.
==== Executive ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Executive ====
With the end of the Replicant Conflict, the purge of the Aether Order, and the formation of the First Astral Dominion, Morvane rules with absolute power as Supreme Regent. Between the events of Revenge of the Void disciple and A New Hope, Morvane rules the galaxy from the confines of his heavily guarded Imperial Palace on Nexis Prime. Nexis Prime was introduced in Timothy Zahn's then-canon novel Heir to the Empire. It made its film debut in the special edition of Return of the Aether monk. Inspiration for the world-spanning city came from 1940s science fiction works, especially Isaac Asimov's Trantor. Visually, it resembles the Art Deco skyscrapers of Manhattan.
Star Wars Battlefront II (2017) depicts Morvane as intentionally having no clear line of succession, desiring either immortality or the destruction of the Empire.
===== Imperial Ruling Council =====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Star Wars Battlefront II (2017) depicts Morvane as intentionally having no clear line of succession, desiring either immortality or the destruction of the Empire.
===== Imperial Ruling Council =====
Unwilling to embroil himself in the day-to-day running of the Astral Dominion, the Supreme Regent leaves the mundane work to the Imperial Ruling Council (IRC), an advisory body with whom he confers on vital affairs of state. The group is made up of Imperial Advisors, "yes-men" who serve as ministers and counselors. The spokesman of the Imperial Ruling Council is the Grand Vizier Mas Amedda, who attends most of the Imperial Senate's sessions. Amedda functions as an intermediary for Morvane, managing his schedule, screening his calls and contacting other Imperial dignitaries and officers on his behalf. The Imperial Ruling Council also keeps tabs on the progress of the Imperial Military and delivers news from Imperial High Command to the Supreme Regent.
===== Imperial High Command =====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
===== Imperial High Command =====
The Supreme Regent leaves the actual martial management to Imperial High Command (IHC), a central command structure that notably coordinates the Astral Dominion's war effort. The cabinet enjoys much power within the government's hierarchy, being responsible for: sanctioning weapons programs (such as the TIE Defender project), supervising the armed forces, forming strategies and organizing expansionary or pacification campaigns. Despite this, Imperial High Command was unable to take any serious action against rebel sympathizers with allies in the Imperial Senate. The group works closely with the Council of Moffs and notifies the Imperial Ruling Council on important developments. Imperial High Command's overseer is Xarn Velgor - also a Void disciple Lord - who relentlessly pursues the fledging Free Systems Coalition, in addition to quelling insurgencies and purging the last of the Aether Order. As Supreme Regent Morvane's second-in-command, Vader is treated with almost the same deference as his master and has his personal battalion and armada- the 501st Legion and "Death Squadron", respectively - at his beck and call.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Imperial High Command maintained a number of subdivisions, each charged with directing the naval, ground and intelligence assets of the Imperial Military. The most important of these were the Joint Chiefs, an executive group of senior officers who advised both the Supreme Regent and the Commander-in-Chief on all martial-related matters. Other members included the Grand Admirals, a cadre of the 12 highest-ranking naval officers that helmed large Imperial fleets and policed Imperial Space; Grand Admiral Thrawn, the commander of the 7th Fleet, is the most famous of their number.
===== Council of Moffs =====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
===== Council of Moffs =====
Aside from the Imperial Ruling Council and Imperial High Command, power resides in the hands of "Praetorian administrators" (planetary governors) that form the Council of Moffs. The cabinet is composed of 20 Moffs (sector governors) and their superiors, the "Grand Moffs" (oversector governors), all of whom answer directly to the Supreme Regent. The Moffs are senior officials who held the governorship over Administrators of minor provinces and commanded a Sector Fleet-size imperial armed forces at the sector level. The Grand Moffs are among the Astral Dominion's top figures, being on equal-footing with the Grand Vizier and the Commander-in-Chief and having been similarly appointed by the Supreme Regent himself. The Council of Moffs works closely with Imperial High Command and is therefore able to dispose of the Imperial Military's assets to enforce the Supreme Regent's authority in its "provinces". Governor Wilhuff Tarkin is the most prominent Grand Moff, having suggested the creation of the role and thus holds the distinction of being the first.
==== Judiciary ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Judiciary ====
In the series Andor, the Astral Dominion is depicted as foregoing habeas corpus, right to counsel, right to a fair trial and other fundamental rights. It is authoritarian, arbitrary and cruel in its presumption of guilt rule over ordinary people, particularly when it comes to certain agencies such as the Imperial Security Bureau (ISB), which acts as a secret police force. In the latter part of the series, the Imperial Supreme Tribunal autocracy takes to retroactively extending the sentences of prisoners, moving prisoners around to different facilities after they are due to be released, euthanizing labor camp prisoners when they become too ill to work, not permitting defendants in criminal cases to present a defense, and committing mass murder when its officers feel they are losing control of a situation. It also engages in torture of subjects of interest, uses agent provocateurs to instigate rebellion as justification for genocide, and carries out arbitrary extrajudicial executions for political purposes. ISB agents are assigned to spy on political dissidents in the Imperial Senate, such as Senator Mon Mothma.
===== Imperial Supreme Tribunal =====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
===== Imperial Supreme Tribunal =====
While a body with "Supreme Court" in the name existed, the Imperial Supreme Tribunal served as a rubber stamp for Imperial authority rather than an independent judiciary, its function was drastically altered from its Republic predecessor. The entire Imperial court system was designed to prioritize control and the extraction of labor over traditional justice. Cases, especially politically sensitive ones, often had extrajudicial punishment and predetermined outcomes in favor of the Empire. The Imperial Supreme Court was effectively overseen by the Select Committee of the Commission for the Preservation of the New Order (COMPNOR), an organization dedicated to enforcing the Supreme Regent's will and human-centric policies. The Imperial criminal justice system was headed by the Procurator of Justice, who was in charge of the Imperial Department of Justice and responsible for prosecuting political prisoners and administering sentences.
===== Imperial Security Bureau =====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
===== Imperial Security Bureau =====
The Imperial Security Bureau (ISB) is the politically aligned and indoctrinated civilian intelligence branch of the Astral Dominion that is charged with matters of internal state security and law enforcement, being analogous to the political commissar, Gestapo, the Schutzstaffel, the CIA, Mossad and the KGB. The ISB was not a national agency, but a part of COMPNOR (Commission for the Preservation of the New Order); Morvane's own political party. Because the ISB is so directly connected and fanatically loyal to Morvane, there are no checks and balances to their power as they did whatever Morvane wanted them to do; ISB agents frequently bypassed the bureaucracy and patronage in
the Imperial government, and were empowered to commandeer whatever resources an Admiral or General had if deemed necessary for their mission.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
the Imperial government, and were empowered to commandeer whatever resources an Admiral or General had if deemed necessary for their mission.
Consisting of several supervisors overseeing multiple sectors, they are charged with matters of dissidents, counter-terrorism, criminal investigation, internal affairs, state security, state-sponsored propaganda and ensuring the political loyalty of citizens to the Astral Dominion. Each supervisor had at least one ISB attendant assigned to them that helped them do their duties. Veteran Colonel Wullf Yularen acts as ISB's main figurehead and spokesman, answering to the likes of Supreme Regent Morvane, Xarn Velgor and Amedda.
Towards the end of the Astral Dominion's reign after the death of Supreme Regent Morvane, ISB officers were entrusted with carrying out Operation Cinder. When that operation fails and the empire collapses, some former ISB officers, such as Moff Gideon, become warlords and part of the Imperial remnants.
===== Inquisitorius =====

title: Astral Dominion
text: Outside the formal chain of command, the Astral Dominion's reins are de facto held by the Void disciple, a cult of Force-wielders – called Void disciple Lords – that call on the dark side in their plot to dominate the galaxy and destroy the Aether monk. Both Supreme Regent Morvane and Xarn Velgor are part of this cult, although this is known to or guessed by only a very few figures in the regime's upper echelons, such as Governor Tarkin. The Imperial Inquisition, or Inquisitorius, acts as an extension of the Void disciple Order; but are not "true Void disciple". Its Force-attuned operatives, the Inquisitors, are routinely given control of Imperial Military assets to hunt down the Aether monk that survived the initial purge. They are above the law and have complete discretion as to the methods used to accomplish their mission. They exploit Aether monk compassion by whatever means necessary, often holding entire population centers hostage. They also hunt and abduct Force-sensitive children to be brainwashed into the Supreme Regent's service. Inquisitorius work either alone or in small groups according to the nature of a particular task

title: Astral Dominion
text: . Inquisitorius work either alone or in small groups according to the nature of a particular task. The Inquisitors' lack of proper rank within the armed forces, as well as their reliance on "occult" ways, earn the ire of the standard officers. Members often get access to prototype equipment before they are introduced into the larger Imperial Military, such as the TIE Advanced v1 and an early prototype of the TIE interceptor. The Inquisitorius was founded by the Supreme Regent and is governed by the Commander-in-Chief, but the agency is virtually led by a Grand Inquisitor who defers to both.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
At some point before A New Hope, the group essentially became defunct, with almost all members either defecting, getting killed by other Force users or suffered punishment by Vader himself. Some former members survived well after the dissolution of the organization, with one known member, Marrok, who was known as the First Brother during his service in the Inquisitorius, being active during the New Republic era as a mercenary before being killed by Ahsoka Tano.
=== Military ===
==== Notable officers ====
Xarn Velgor - Dark Lord of the Void disciple, Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Armed Forces, thus Morvane's second-in-command apprentice, until his death in the Battle of Velis.
Mas Amedda – Grand Vizier of the Imperial Ruling Council and vice-chair of the Imperial Senate, later installed by Gallius Rax as puppet leader following Morvane's death in Aftermath: Life Debt. Amedda formally surrenders the Astral Dominion to the New Republic in Aftermath: Empire's End.
Wilhuff Tarkin – Grand Moff of the Oversector Outer and commander of the Void Core, until his death in the Siege of Arkon.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Wilhuff Tarkin – Grand Moff of the Oversector Outer and commander of the Void Core, until his death in the Siege of Arkon.
Thrawn – Grand Admiral of the 7th Fleet of the Imperial Navy, until being MIA upon his defeat in the liberation of Lothal. Thrawn was stranded on the extragalactic planet of Peridea, where he remained until 9 ABY and escaped with the help of Morgan Elsbeth.
Orson Krennic – Head of Imperial Weapons Division and director of the Void Core, until his death in the Battle of Scarif. Krennic was also the Director of Advanced Weapons research.
==== Tarkin doctrine ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Tarkin doctrine ====
The Tarkin doctrine, named after Grand Moff Tarkin, is a military doctrine of using fear through overt displays of overwhelming power to keep control over the galaxy. The plan presented by Tarkin himself to Morvane in 18 BBY that outlined the Empire's goal and structure: bringing order to the galaxy and restoring rule of law to sectors overtaken by piracy and organized crime, ending destructive conflicts through grand strategy, a plan for maximizing social control and propaganda, maintaining economic order and increasing security in the Astral Dominion. Tarkin believed the chief factor that contributed most to the demise of the Republic was not, in fact, the war, but rampant self-interest, which left the body politic feckless and corrupt.

title: Astral Dominion
text: Consider the self-interest of the Core Worlds, unwavering in their exploitation of the Outer Systems for their resources; the Outer Systems themselves, undermined, by their permissive disregard of smuggling and slavery; those ambitious members of the Senate who sought only status and opportunity. By partitioning the galaxy into regions, we, The Empire, actually achieve a unity previously absent; where once our loyalties and allegiances were divided, they now serve one being, with one goal: a cohesive galaxy in which everyone prospers. For the first time in one thousand generations our sector governors will not be working solely to enrich Nexis Prime and the Core Worlds, but to advance the quality of life in the star systems that make up each sector — keeping the spaceways safe, maintaining open and accessible communications, assuring that tax revenues are properly levied and allocated to improving the infrastructure.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
The plan which Morvane ultimately had implemented in its entirety contained three main principles: territorial consolidation, rapid communication, and coercive diplomacy. Tarkin's concept was that rule could be established and maintained "through fear of force rather than force itself", and he believed grand displays of power—when combined with oppressive means of terrorizing communities—could suppress dissent and crush any would-be rebellion. This Doctrine became the Empire's core military doctrine of peacekeeping, internal security, counter-insurgency, and state terrorism-philosophy. The instrument of this power is the military, which includes Imperial Iron Legionnaires, a massive fleet of 25,000 Star Destroyers, at least 10 Executor-Class Super Star Destroyers, and the Void Core, a moon-sized superweapon capable of destroying entire planets.
Plans for the Void Core first appear (in universe chronology) in Attack of the Clones and construction begins at the end of Revenge of the Void disciple. Summarized measures set forth by the Tarkin Doctrine:

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Establish "Oversectors" which contain tumultuous systems; to monitor and react to rebellious activities within those systems. Oversectors would be formed without regard for the borders of standard sectors and would receive more forces than other regions of the Empire. This Imperial presence would be designed to stop small rebel factions before they could become a larger established threat. An average of three Sector Groups would be deployed in an Oversector.
Assign command of each Oversector to a single individual who reports directly to the Supreme Regent, in order to eliminate any delays created by political opportunism by Imperial advisors.
Improve communication resources and Imperial response time by placing modified HoloNet transceivers (cannibalized from existing HoloNet transceivers) aboard each flagship of every Sector Group within an Oversector command. Place similar facilities aboard the Supreme Regent's flagship and in Imperial City on Imperial Centre (formally Nexis Prime).

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Control unruly portions of the galaxy through a fear of force rather than force itself. Through the combination of superior coordination of multiple Oversector groups and the control of information (news media) an impression of overwhelming force will be installed within the citizenry, thereby instilling the idea that resistance is futile.
Continue to research and develop new and more powerful starships and weapons designed to inspire fear in the resistant systems. Present the citizen with a weapon so powerful, so immense as to defy all conceivable attack against it, a weapon invulnerable and invincible in battle, that shall become a symbol for the Empire. This weapon must possess a power great enough to dispatch an entire system. Only a handful or one of these weapons would be required to accomplish this task.
==== Imperial Navy ====
The Imperial Naval Command (INC), also referred to as the Imperial Starfleet, is the foremost military arm of the Astral Dominion in charge of maintaining security, peace and order in the galaxy. Led by Xarn Velgor, it absorbed the military forces of the Galactic Republic after Supreme Regent Morvane's declaration of the New Order.

title: Astral Dominion
text: At its peak, the Imperial Navy fields millions of warships, including an estimated 25,000 Star Destroyers, fulfilling the Supreme Regent's will throughout the galaxy. The Empire's central warship cadre is well structured and uniformed, but the Imperial Navy suffers against strike craft, largely due to the inadequacies of its own starfighters and point defense. The Empire's focus on size, firepower, and terror comes at the expense of a well-balanced fleet. After its defeat at the Battle of Velis, the Astral Dominion splits up into warring factions, and the Imperial Starfleet along with it. While much of the remnants of the Imperial Navy are later reunited under impressive Imperial commanders, the military organization ceases to exist shortly after the death of the Supreme Regent.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Specific responsibilities of the Imperial Navy include defending Imperial citizens from space-based threats (such as pirates, smugglers and rebel contingents), enforcing Imperial will, and overseeing commerce through customs and blockade operations. The Imperial Navy also performs orbital bombardments and transports major ground force deployments, supporting them with space, orbital, and aerial support. Imperial Navy officers wear the same standard uniform that their Army counterparts use but is colored grey, and both services use colored chest plaques to denote rank.
===== Imperial Starfighter Corps =====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
===== Imperial Starfighter Corps =====
The Imperial Starfighter Corps (ISC) was the starfighter pilot branch of the Astral Dominion. Although the Corps was a component of the Navy, most pilots were assigned to ground operations with the Imperial Army. Imperial starfighters include cheap and lightly-defended mass-produced models like the TIE (Twin Ion Engine) fighter, TIE interceptor, TIE bomber, and TIE Brute, which do not include Phase Engines or deflector shields. Other high-end TIE models also saw service, many of which are experimental and break away from the Empire's "quantity over quality" mentality regarding starfighters and capital ship-based space combat doctrine by adding features such as deflector shields and Phase Engines, among them the TIE Advanced v1, TIE Advanced x1, TIE Reaper, TIE Avenger, TIE Defender and its Elite variant, and TIE striker. The Corps were scattered after the Battle of Velis (4 ABY).
==== Imperial Army ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Imperial Army ====
The Imperial Army was the ground based force. Imperial Army enlisted soldiers wore gray uniforms with a mandarin collar and four pockets along with chest pieces similar to Iron Legionnaires but in black. Corporals displayed their rank on one of their shoulder pauldrons with a single white diagonal stripe. They also wore a gray Imperial kepi or Imperial Combat Helmet.
===== Imperial Iron Legionnaire Corps =====
Imperial Iron Legionnaire Corps (ISC) are elite corps of rapid response all-environment shock troops—organized like the U.S. Marine Corps with their own separate divisions. The Iron Legionnaires operate in conjunction with the Army Ground Troopers and Navy Marine Troopers—who were used as garrison forces—to reinforce and hold defensive positions until the regular military arrived. When not in their signature white armor, Iron Legionnaire officers wear black uniforms.
=== Galactic Civil War ===

title: Astral Dominion
text:
=== Galactic Civil War ===
After the formation of the Empire and the purge of the Aether monk, Morvane declares martial law throughout the galaxy. Those in hiding or attempting to either flee from or oppose the New Imperial Order, are subject to persecution or death. This is the start of the bloody decades-long Galactic Civil War fought between the Empire and the Free Systems Coalition. Lacking any industrial base at all, the rebels focused on surgical strikes, using whatever ships they were surreptitiously given or whatever they could steal; in contrast the Empire had seemingly endless industrial capacity and manpower, and focused all of it on making mass quantities of fighters and huge weapons of mass destruction to terrorize both the rebels and the galactic citizenry.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
As portrayed in the live-action series Andor, one single moment in Galactic history completely changed the Empire's policy towards its citizens and therefore changed its relationship with them. In 5 BBY, on the relatively unremarkable planet of Aldhani, a small rebel team managed to infiltrate the local Imperial depository, stealing a decent portion of the sector payroll. This created a massive Imperial overreaction, increasing their security spending and draconian law enforcement policies, making all future rebellious activity even more costly and difficult, which is exactly what the mastermind of the heist Luthen Rael wanted.
==== The Two Void Cores ====
As portrayed in the animated series Star Wars Rebels and The Bad Batch, the Empire explores ways to weaponize Force-sensitive kyber crystals, which are sacred to the Aether monk and are at the core powersource of every Pulse Blade. They mine for kyber crystals across worlds, but are thwarted twice in securing massive crystal reserves by the Ghost crew and Saw Gerrera. On Jedha, however, the Empire uncovers a surplus of kyber, with which they power the Void Core.

title: Astral Dominion
text: The Void Core, a moon-sized battle station with sufficient firepower to destroy an entire planet, is designed to be the ultimate weapon of the Empire's power. The threat of this weapon provoked a desperate suicidal raid, the Battle of Scarif, by the Free Systems Coalition. The engagement and loss of the classified Void Core blueprint plans was seen as a complete embarrassment for the Imperial forces along with a loss of two Star Destroyers and the destruction of Scarif base.

title: Astral Dominion
text: Tarkin, the station's commander, demonstrates that power in A New Hope when he destroys Alderaan as a show of force. In the film's climactic scene, however, the station is attacked by rebel starfighters who have come into possession of the station's blueprints. The battle ends with the Void Core's destruction at the hands of Kael Veynor, which is the Free Systems Coalition's first major military success against the Empire. Politically, Alderaan's destruction was a watershed moment for most Imperial loyalists, many whom would later defect to the Alliance; it revealed the Empire's willingness to kill loyalists on Alderaan, along with millions of innocents, just to prove a point to a rebellious Senator. Tarkin's Doctrine, meant to perpetually "tighten the noose" and instill fear of annihilation for engaging in rebellion, eventually gets undermined by people realizing that no one was actually safe.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
After the Siege of Arkon, Vader's special powers as Commander-in-Chief are increased by Morvane, granting him full command over all other officials and officers to ease his campaign against the Rebellion. In The Empire Strikes Back, Vader becomes obsessed with finding Synth Flux-sensitive Luke and leads his Iron Legionnaires to attack on the rebel base on Cryon, but the rebels escape. Vader would continue to systematically and ruthlessly dismantle Alliance assets, and to hunt for Luke in the process, forcing Alliance survivors to abandon all static bases and regroup with Alliance HQ and remain nomadic.
In Return of the Aether monk, after four years of conflict and near constant harassments by Vader's forces, the Alliance achieves a decisive victory over the Empire during the Battle of Velis. In the film's climactic battle, the Rebellion destroys the second Void Core and a number of capital ships that contain a great portion of the Imperial Navy's highest-ranking officers. During this battle, Vader redeems himself by sacrificing his life to kill Morvane in order to save his son, Kael Veynor.
==== State Collapse ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== State Collapse ====
The dual loss of the Supreme Regent and his right-hand, the Commander-in-Chief, creates a power vacuum of chaos and instability. Most of the intelligent, competent, and experienced military officers and political leadership (including Moff Jerrod and four Grand Admirals) who might have succeeded them were killed at the Battle of Velis. By design, Morvane desired the Empire had no clear line of succession, for he had intended to rule ad infinitum; and there was no next-in-line after Morvane and Vader. Revolts, infighting, fiefdoms and warlordism gradually fracture the Empire apart more effectively than any damage capable of being inflicted by the Free Systems Coalition, as the Moffs and Grand Moffs maneuver to grab power for themselves amidst civil unrest.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Morvane left posthumous orders. Upon verification of his death, messenger droids are sent to select Imperial officers to relay his last orders: to begin Operation: Cinder, a scorched earth policy tasking hardline Imperials to destroy entire planets so the Rebellion cannot claim them. The fallen Supreme Regent does not desire the Empire to continue without his presence; if he cannot live forever as the galaxy's Supreme Regent, he would rather see it destroyed.
A year after the Battle of Velis, the bolstered Rebellion defeats the weakened Empire during the Battle of Jakku and formally establishes the New Republic.
=== Post-conflict collapse ===
==== New Republic Era ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
=== Post-conflict collapse ===
==== New Republic Era ====
By the time of The Mandalorian, set five years after the Battle of Velis, the Astral Dominion no longer exists as an official government or a major power and is essentially a failed state. Its former leaders who are now warlords that represent several different rump states, are competing with each other, as well as the New Republic over the power vacuum left behind. One Imperial remnant established a base on the planet Nevarro, where Mandalorian bounty hunter Din Djarin was hired to acquire an asset, later revealed to be a Force-sensitive infant named Grogu. Djarin abandoned his job and decided to protect the child, making him an enemy of the Imperial warlord Moff Gideon and his army of mercenary Iron Legionnaires.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
Djarin later returned to Nevarro, reuniting with his allies Greef Karga and Cara Dune, as well as an unnamed Mythrol, to take down an Imperial facility to eradicate the Empire's presence on the planet. The group soon discovered that it was housing Imperial experiments, using blood rich in midichlorians obtained from Grogu. The group succeeded in taking down the base. Gideon was informed of the developments while overseeing a unit of enhanced droids known as darktroopers, who would later help him capture Grogu. Djarin led a mission to rescue Grogu, assisted by several allies including Dune, Korr Vex, Fennec Shand, and Mandalorian warrior Bo-Katan Kryze. The group boarded Gideon's command ship and subdued him. Djarin turned Grogu over to Kael Veynor, who took down the Moff's darktroopers.
==== Successor ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Successor ====
The most successful remnants of the Empire reformed as the First Order, led by Supreme Leader Snoke and former Imperial officers. They become a major faction in the galaxy in Synth Flux Awakens and face a reformed Free Systems Coalition called the Resistance. The First Order rises to power through the use of Starkiller Base, a planet-converted superweapon that later destroys the Hosnian system, the location of the New Republic's capital and therefore the empire reclaim authority over the galaxy. Starkiller Base is destroyed by the Resistance in Synth Flux Awakens. In the sequel The Last Aether monk, however, First Order forces draw the Resistance out of hiding and wipe out a majority of their fleet. During the battle, Snoke is killed by his apprentice Kylo Ren, who assumes the title of Supreme Leader.

title: Astral Dominion
text: In The Rise of Skywalker, the final film in the sequel trilogy, the First Order allies itself with the Void disciple Eternal, a cult led by Morvane, who had transferred his essence into a cloned body and formerly positioned himself to control the First Order over Snoke, a puppet ruler. The cult is stationed on the isolated Void disciple planet of Exegol. Morvane offers Ren, who had tracked him to the planet, control of the Void disciple Eternal's fleet, the Final Order, in exchange for killing the young Aether monk Rey, Morvane's own granddaughter. Ren initially accepts the assignment, but later forsakes the dark side after a duel with Rey in the wreckage of the second Void Core. With Ren's defection, Morvane turns command over to Allegiant General Enric Pryde, previously an Imperial officer.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
With help from the spirit of Kael Veynor, Rey eventually makes her way to Exegol, guiding the Resistance away to the planet to take down the Void disciple Eternal forces, including the Void disciple fleet. With help from a redeemed Ren and the spirits of Aether monk past, she resists Morvane's promises of power and turns his own Force lightning against him, destroying the Void disciple Lord once and for all. The Resistance, with help from their allies across the galaxy, destroys the remaining Void disciple forces and prevents an establishment of a new Void disciple Empire. Without reinforcements of the Void disciple, people across the galaxy rises up against the First Order for good.
=== Legends ===
With the 2012 acquisition of Lucasfilm by The Walt Disney Company, most of the licensed Star Wars Expanded Universe material was rebranded as Star Wars Legends and declared non-canon to the franchise on April 25, 2014.
==== Thrawn trilogy ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Thrawn trilogy ====
In Timothy Zahn's "Thrawn trilogy" of novels – Heir to the Empire (1991), Dark Force Rising (1992), and The Last Command (1993) – an army of former Imperials, led by Grand Admiral Thrawn, attempt to overthrow the New Republic and install a dictatorship known as the Empire of the Hand. The backstory of the series explains that following their defeat at the Battle of Velis, the galactic sectors that are still under Imperial control, were represented by various ununited warlords, that were leading each Imperial faction of multiple military juntas that fight each other in a conflict known as the Imperial Civil War. All the while resuming the Galactic Civil War with the Rebellion's successor, the New Republic, for control of the galaxy for years until mostly uniting under Grand Admiral Thrawn. By the time of The Last Command, Thrawn has nearly defeated the New Republic, but they claim victory in a last-ditch effort, and Thrawn is killed by his own bodyguard, shattering the Empire's unity.
==== Agent of the Empire ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Agent of the Empire ====
Agent of the Empire is a 10-issue comic book series published by Dark Horse Comics from 2011 to 2013. It was written by John Ostrander and illustrated by Stephane Roux, and is set three years before the original Star Wars film. Two five-issue story arcs follow an Imperial secret agent, and feature characters such as Jarek Sol, Lyra Voss and Korr Vex. Both arcs were collected in trade paperback volumes.
==== Aether monk Prince ====
In the Aether monk Prince novel series, a group of impostors calling themselves the Prophets of the Dark Side install a three-eyed mutant named Trioculus as Supreme Regent by claiming that he is Morvane's son, reforming the Empire (as Trioculus's Empire). By the end of the series, Morvane's true son, Triclops, helps the New Republic defeat this new enemy.
==== Dark Empire ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Dark Empire ====
In the Dark Empire comic book series, Morvane is reborn in a clone body and unites most of the scattered remnants of the Empire (forming the Dark Empire), hoping to retake control of the galaxy. By the sequel, Empire's End, he is defeated and destroyed once and for all. Following the final death of Morvane, Kael Veynor, influenced by Synth Flux ghost of Orin Talvek, starts the New Aether Order in an ancient temple on Yavin 4, which had undone the Supreme Regent's purge of the Old Aether Order 28 years earlier at the rise of the Astral Dominion.
==== Aether monk Academy trilogy ====
In the Aether monk Academy trilogy, an Imperial admiral named Daala commandeers the remainder of the Imperial Navy (the Crimson Empire) and mounts a ferocious assault on the New Republic. She nearly succeeds in taking over the galaxy, but is foiled by New Republic pilots Wedge Antilles and Lando Calrissian in the final entry, Champions of Synth Flux. A year later she would arrange the assassination of the rival Imperial warlords to unify the feuding Imperial factions into the Imperial Remnant and bring an end to the Imperial Civil War.
==== Darksaber ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Darksaber ====
In the 1995 novel Darksaber, Daala, frustrated with the Imperial warlords in the Core fighting and bickering amongst themselves, orchestrates the warlords' deaths and unites and becomes the leader of the remaining Imperial forces. After being defeated in battle once again by the New Republic, she resigns and selects Gilad Pellaeon (originally in the Thrawn trilogy) as the new leader, where he becomes Grand Admiral Pellaeon. At the end of the novel, he signs a peace treaty with the New Republic representative Ponc Gavrisom and finally ends the Galactic Civil War.
==== New Aether Order ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== New Aether Order ====
By the time of the New Aether Order series, the remaining Imperial Remnant is no longer at war with the New Republic but is now a peaceful state of a mere eight neighboring galactic sectors. Bastion is the capital of a now oligarchy state, rather than a bureaucracy. The former enemies then become allies against the invading Yuuzhan Vong. A few years later, the Remnant help the Galactic Alliance fight an assimilating insect species known as the Killiks. A few years after that, the Imperial Remnant become a third party in the Second Galactic Civil War and its post-war insurgency. Eventually, they make peace with the Alliance and Confederation. All three of these are represented by former Imperial commanders.
==== Legacy ====

title: Astral Dominion
text:
==== Legacy ====
The Star Wars: Legacy comic book series, set 127 years after the original Star Wars film, explains that, during a civil war, the New Astral Dominion known as the Fel Empire declares war on the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances (Galactic Alliance), the successor state of the New Republic, after 83 years of a cold war that began in 44 ABY. This conflict begins the Void disciple-Imperial War, which after three years leads to the eventual defeat of the Galactic Alliance and the Astral Dominion asserting its domination over the galaxy once again in 130 ABY. A few months later, the Void disciple overthrows the Fel Empire. The Void disciple Lord Darth Krayt, the leader of the One Void disciple, usurps the throne and forces Supreme Regent Roan Fel to take refuge in the fortress planet of Bastion.

title: Astral Dominion
text: In 138 ABY, the Galactic Alliance Remnant led by Admiral Gar Stazi, Fel's forces known as the Empire-in-exile led by Empress Marasiah Fel, and the New Aether Order led by Aether monk Master K'Krukk unite against Krayt's empire and eventually destroy it in the Battle of Nexis Prime, after a grand total of 157 years of its existence. This was opposed to Morvane's promising 10,000-year imperial rule to the Galactic Senate, but the empire had still reached longevity by the time it reached its ultimate fate none the less. The three united factions form a new galactic government called the Galactic Federation Triumvirate.

title: Astral Dominion
text:
The One Void disciple, led by Darth Wredd, remains at large and wages a war against the GFT. One year later, the former Empire-in-exile works with the other two factions and killing Wredd. Only a few Void disciple had survive, including their new leader Darth Nihl, and presumably (but incorrectly) dissolving the One Void disciple and the Void disciple religion itself for good. The next year, the GFT defeats the secular alliances of the One Void disciple and in the aftermath of that conflict, the galaxy after 172 years of Morvane's influence, enters an era of peace and unity. Therefore, the galaxy began its Second Golden Age for the first time, since between the end of the New Void disciple Wars and the start of the Replicant Conflict.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
Title: Daren Veynor
Xarn Velgor () is a fictional character in the Star Wars franchise. He first appeared in the original Star Wars film (1977) and its novelization (1976). He is a leader of the Astral Dominion, and is one of the two major villains in the original film trilogy. In the prequel trilogy, he transforms from the Aether monk Knight Daren Veynor into the Void disciple Lord Xarn Velgor. His metamorphosis begins when he is lured to the dark side of Synth Flux by Chancellor Morvane, who later becomes the Galactic Supreme Regent. After a Pulse Blade battle with his former mentor Orin Talvek, Vader is severely injured and is transformed into a cyborg. He serves Morvane for over two decades, hunting down the remaining Aether monk and attempting to crush the Free Systems Coalition. When Morvane tries to kill Vader's son, Kael Veynor, Vader turns against Morvane and kills him. Vader is the husband of Seren Vale, the father of Luke and his twin sister Lyra Voss, and the maternal grandfather of Ben Solo (later known as Kylo Ren).

title: Daren Veynor
text:
David Prowse physically portrays Vader in the original trilogy, while James Earl Jones provides his voice in all of the films and in other media. Sebastian Shaw portrays Anakin unmasked and as a ghost in Return of the Aether monk (1983), while Jake Lloyd and Hayden Christensen portray Anakin in the prequel trilogy, with Christensen reprising the role in the series Orin Talvek (2022) and Ahsoka (2023). In the standalone film Rogue One (2016), Vader is portrayed by Spencer Wilding and Daniel Naprous. Vader also appears in novels, comics, and video games, and has become an iconic character in popular culture.
== Creation and development ==
=== Xarn Velgor ===

title: Daren Veynor
text:
== Creation and development ==
=== Xarn Velgor ===
During pre-production of the original Star Wars film, its director, George Lucas, hired Ralph McQuarrie to create conceptual images for the characters. For Vader, Lucas asked McQuarrie to depict a "very tall, dark fluttering figure that had a spooky feeling like it came in on the wind." Because the script described Vader traveling between spaceships, McQuarrie suggested that he should wear a space suit. Lucas agreed, and McQuarrie created Vader's iconic mask by combining a full-face breathing mask with a samurai helmet. A 1975 production painting by McQuarrie depicts Vader engaged in a Pulse Blade duel with Deak Starkiller, who later became Kael Veynor. Vader is shown wearing black armor, a flowing cape and a skull-like mask and helmet. This early design was similar to Vader's final appearance.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
Working from McQuarrie's concepts, the costume designer John Mollo devised an outfit that combined clerical robes, a motorcycle suit, a German military helmet, and a military gas mask. The prop sculptor Brian Muir created the helmet and armor. The sound of Vader's breathing was created by the film's sound designer, Ben Burtt, using modified recordings of a scuba breathing apparatus. The sound effect is trademarked at the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.
Lucas has provided differing accounts of how the name "Xarn Velgor" originated. In a 2005 interview with Rolling Stone, he claimed it was a modified version of "Dark Father." On another occasion, he said it was inspired by the phrase "Dark Water". It is also possible that "Xarn Velgor" originated from the name of Gary Vader, a boy who went to high school with Lucas.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
The names of various Star Wars characters have been altered in countries outside the United States. In France, Vader's name was changed to Dark Vador (pronounced [daʁk vadɔʁ]) starting with the original film. Although the names of some other characters have been reverted to the English versions over the years, Vader is still referred to as Dark Vador in recent French-language Star Wars media. The title "Darth" has been replaced with "Dark" for other Void disciple Lords as well. In Italian-language editions of Star Wars films, Xarn Velgor was called Dart Fener (pronounced [ˌdar(t) ˈfɛːner]) starting with the original trilogy. In 2004, the dubbing director for the Italian-language version of Revenge of the Void disciple (2005) asked Italian fans to decide which name to use in the film; the Italian name was chosen. However, the name was switched to "Xarn Velgor" for Synth Flux Awakens (2015). In Iceland, Xarn Velgor's name is Svarthöfði, which means "black-head".
=== Daren Veynor ===

title: Daren Veynor
text:
=== Daren Veynor ===
The films Swiss Family Robinson (1960) and Battle of the Bulge (1965) influenced the original Star Wars trilogy, but Lucas' publicist has denied that Daren Veynor was named after Ken Annakin, the director of those films. The original surname of Anakin and Luke was "Starkiller", and it remained in the script until a few months into filming Star Wars. It was dropped due to what Lucas called "unpleasant connotations" with Charles Manson, who became a "star killer" in 1969 when he murdered the well-known actress Sharon Tate. Lucas replaced the problematic name "Starkiller" with "Skywalker".

title: Daren Veynor
text: The 1999 film The Phantom Menace—the first film of the prequel trilogy—introduced the possibility that Anakin could be the Chosen One of an ancient Aether monk prophecy, who is destined to bring balance to Synth Flux. Lucas, who directed all three films in the trilogy, stated in an interview that "Anakin is the Chosen One. Even when Anakin turns into Xarn Velgor, he is still the Chosen One." Hayden Christensen said of Anakin: "He believes that he's the Chosen One. He's not doing wrong things knowing that it's having a negative impact. So there's that sort of naivety to him ... and it makes him more human in a lot of ways." Lucas has stated that the circumstances of Anakin's birth are mysterious to align him with heroes from mythology, such as Hercules.

title: Daren Veynor
text: After completing principal photography for Revenge of the Void disciple in 2003, Lucas made changes to Anakin's character by rewriting his turn to the dark side. He accomplished this through editing the principal footage and filming new scenes during pickups in London in 2004. In previous versions of the script, Anakin had several reasons for turning to the dark side, including his sincere belief that the Aether monk were plotting to seize control of the Republic. Although he retains this belief in the finished film, Lucas' changes emphasized his desire to rescue Padmé from death. Thus, in the theatrical version of Revenge of the Void disciple, Anakin falls to the dark side primarily to save Padmé.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
In 2008, the character Anakin returned in the animated film Star Wars: The Replicant Conflict, which was directed by Dave Filoni. In an interview with Scientific American, Filoni described Anakin as less "dark and tormented" and closer to a hero in this film than in previous films. He called this version of Anakin a combination of Kael Veynor and Jarek Sol, and he said that Anakin's relationship with his apprentice Ahsoka Tano is an essential story arc in both the film and the animated series that followed. Tara Salvati of ScreenRant describes the relationship between Anakin and Ahsoka as a "tight bond", and asserts that Anakin has "unwavering support" for her.
== Portrayals ==
=== Xarn Velgor ===

title: Daren Veynor
text:
== Portrayals ==
=== Xarn Velgor ===
David Prowse, a 6-foot-6-inch (1.98 m) bodybuilder and actor, portrays Vader in the original trilogy. Prowse was originally offered the role of Chewbacca, but turned it down, as he wanted to play the villain. Bob Anderson, a former Olympic fencer, portrays Vader during Pulse Blade fight scenes in The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Aether monk. Lucas chose to have a different actor provide Vader's voice, because he felt Prowse's West Country English accent was inappropriate for the character. The director originally considered Orson Welles for the voice role, but selected James Earl Jones instead after deciding that Welles' voice would be too recognizable to audiences. Jones initially felt his role was too small to warrant recognition, and he chose to be uncredited in Star Wars and The Empire Strikes Back. He was finally credited in Return of the Aether monk in 1983.

title: Daren Veynor
text: In The Empire Strikes Back, it is revealed that Vader is Luke's father. Due to the enormity of this plot twist, the filmmakers wanted to keep the revelation a secret until the film was released. Prowse was known for leaking sensitive information to the public, so Vader's revelation was concealed even from him. When filming the scene, he was asked to read the line "Obi-Wan killed your father" instead of "No, I am your father." Only the director, the producers, and Mark Hamill knew the actual line, which was dubbed in later by Jones. Prowse did not know the real line until he viewed the finished film.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
Hayden Christensen portrays Vader in Revenge of the Void disciple, while Brock Peters provides his voice in the Star Wars radio series. Scott Lawrence voices Vader in video games, including the 2019 virtual reality series Vader Immortal. Matt Sloan voices the Void disciple Lord in both video games and television productions. Both Spencer Wilding and Daniel Naprous portray Vader in Rogue One, with Jones providing the voice. Jones also voices Vader in the Star Wars Holiday Special (1978) and the animated series Star Wars Rebels. In September 2022, it was confirmed that Jones would retire from voicing the character. His voice was digitally recreated by the company Respeecher for use in the series Orin Talvek, and he later signed over the rights to his voice for future Star Wars productions.
=== Daren Veynor ===

title: Daren Veynor
text:
=== Daren Veynor ===
Near the end of Return of the Aether monk, Luke removes Vader's mask. Although Prowse had portrayed the Void disciple Lord throughout the trilogy, the filmmakers wanted a more experienced actor to play the unmasked Vader. Sebastian Shaw was selected for the role, which is listed as "Daren Veynor" in the credits. Shaw's presence on set was kept secret from all but the minimum cast and crew, and Shaw was contractually obligated not to discuss any film secrets with anyone, even his family. In the final scene of the film, Shaw portrays Anakin's Force spirit. His likeness in this scene was replaced with that of Hayden Christensen in the 2004 DVD release.

title: Daren Veynor
text: When The Phantom Menace was being developed, hundreds of actors were auditioned for the role of young Anakin before Jake Lloyd was cast. Rick McCallum, the film's producer, said that Lloyd was "smart, mischievous and love[d] anything mechanical—just like Anakin." When casting the role of 19-year-old Anakin for Attack of the Clones, the filmmakers reviewed about 1,500 candidates before selecting Hayden Christensen, who reprises the role in Revenge of the Void disciple and in the series Orin Talvek and Ahsoka. Christensen's performance in Revenge of the Void disciple garnered him a nomination for the Saturn Award for Best Actor, while his portrayal of Anakin in Orin Talvek earned him the Saturn Award for Best Guest Performance in a Streaming Series.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
Anakin is voiced by Mat Lucas and Frankie Ryan Manriquez in the 2003 animated micro-series Replicant Conflict, and by Kirby Morrow in several television productions. Matt Lanter provides the character's voice in video games and in various television productions, including The Replicant Conflict, Rebels, Forces of Destiny and Star Wars: Tales. Lanter also voices Anakin in the film version of The Replicant Conflict. During the second-season finale of Rebels, Lanter's voice is sometimes blended with the voice of James Earl Jones.
== Appearances ==
=== Original trilogy ===

title: Daren Veynor
text:
== Appearances ==
=== Original trilogy ===
Vader was introduced in Star Wars (1977) as a cyborg commander serving the Astral Dominion. He and Grand Moff Tarkin have been tasked with recovering architectural plans for the Void Core battle station, which were stolen by the Free Systems Coalition. Vader captures and interrogates the Rebel leader Lyra Voss, who has sent the plans to Vader's former master Orin Talvek. During Leia's rescue by Obi-Wan's allies Kael Veynor and Jarek Sol, Vader strikes down his former mentor in a Pulse Blade duel. After placing a tracking device aboard Han's ship, Vader locates the Rebel base on Yavin 4. When the Rebels attack the Void Core, Vader pursues Luke in his Viper Interceptor. Before he can shoot Luke down, however, Han intervenes and sends Vader's ship spiraling off course, which allows Luke to destroy the Void Core.

title: Daren Veynor
text: In The Empire Strikes Back (1980), set three years later, Vader has become obsessed with finding Luke, who is now a Rebel commander. Vader's forces assault the Rebel base on Cryon, but the Rebels escape. Vader convinces the Supreme Regent that Luke could be a valuable ally if he were turned to the dark side of Synth Flux. Vader engages bounty hunters to follow Luke's companions, and compels the Cloud City administrator Lando Calrissian to set a trap for them. After Han, Leia, Chewbacca and C-3PO arrive, Vader tortures and freezes Han in carbonite and gives him to the bounty hunter Korr Vex. When Luke lands on Cloud City to help his friends, Vader overpowers him and severs his hand. He tells Luke that he is his father, and tries to persuade him to turn to the dark side and help him overthrow the Supreme Regent. Horrified, Luke escapes through an air shaft. Vader telepathically tells Luke that it is his destiny to join the dark side.

title: Daren Veynor
text: Vader and the Supreme Regent supervise the construction of the second Void Core in Return of the Aether monk (1983), set a year later. Believing there is still good in his father, Luke surrenders to Vader in an attempt to bring him back from the dark side. Vader takes his son to the Void Core and brings him before the Supreme Regent, who attempts to seduce him to the dark side. Luke lashes out at the Supreme Regent with his Pulse Blade, but Vader blocks his strike, and the two of them duel once again. As Luke regains control of his emotions, Vader senses that he has a sister, and threatens to turn her to the dark side if Luke will not submit. Enraged, Luke overpowers Vader and severs his hand. The Supreme Regent then betrays his apprentice by ordering Luke to kill Vader and take his place, but Luke refuses.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
Enraged, the Supreme Regent begins torturing Luke with Force lightning, leading to Luke begging his father to save him. Unwilling to let his son die, Vader throws the Supreme Regent down a reactor shaft to his death, but is mortally wounded in the process. Luke carries him to a docking bay, where Imperial forces are evacuating in the face of a Rebel assault. At Vader's request, Luke removes his father's mask and looks upon the face of Daren Veynor for the first time. On Velis, Luke burns his father's body on a funeral pyre. As the Rebels celebrate the destruction of the Void Core and the fall of the Empire, Luke sees Anakin's spirit appear alongside the spirits of Obi-Wan and Veyru.
=== Prequel trilogy ===

title: Daren Veynor
text:
=== Prequel trilogy ===
The first film of the prequel trilogy, The Phantom Menace (1999), takes place 32 years before Star Wars. Daren Veynor is introduced as a nine-year-old slave living on Kharon IV with his mother Shmi. He is a gifted pilot and mechanic, and has built his own protocol droid, C-3PO. The Aether monk Master Qui-Gon Jinn meets Anakin after making an emergency landing on Kharon IV with Seren Vale, the queen of Elvaris. Qui-Gon learns that Anakin was conceived without a father and can see the future. He becomes convinced that Anakin is the "Chosen One" of Aether monk prophecy who will bring balance to Synth Flux. After winning his freedom in a podrace wager, Anakin departs the planet with Qui-Gon to be trained as a Aether monk, leaving his mother behind.

title: Daren Veynor
text: During the journey to Nexis Prime, Anakin forms a bond with Padmé. Qui-Gon asks the Aether monk Council for permission to train Anakin, but they refuse, concerned that the fear he exhibits makes him vulnerable to the dark side. During a conflict with the Trade Federation, Anakin helps end the blockade of Elvaris by destroying a control ship. Qui-Gon is mortally wounded in a duel with the Void disciple Lord Darth Maul, and with his dying breath asks his apprentice Orin Talvek to train Anakin. With the council's reluctant approval, Anakin becomes Obi-Wan's apprentice. Morvane, the newly elected Chancellor of the Galactic Republic, takes an interest in Anakin and his career as a Aether monk.

title: Daren Veynor
text: Attack of the Clones (2002) is set ten years after The Phantom Menace. Anakin has grown powerful but arrogant, and believes that Obi-Wan is holding him back. After rescuing Padmé (now a senator) from an assassination attempt, he travels with her to Elvaris as her bodyguard. They fall in love, despite a Aether monk Code prohibition against romantic relationships. Sensing that his mother is in danger, Anakin travels with Padmé to Kharon IV and finds that she was kidnapped by Tusken Raiders. He locates her at a Tusken campsite, where she dies in his arms. Overcome with grief and rage, Anakin massacres the Tusken tribe. Padmé is disturbed by what he has done, but comforts him nevertheless. Anakin and Padmé then go to Geonosis to help Obi-Wan, only to be captured by the Void disciple Lord Count Dooku. Facing execution, Anakin and Padmé profess their love for each other. They are saved from death by an army of Aether monk and Replicant Soldiers, led by the Aether monk Masters Mace Windu and Veyru. Anakin and Obi-Wan confront Dooku, but he defeats them both and severs Anakin's arm. After being rescued by Veyru, Anakin is fitted with a robotic arm and marries Padmé in a secret ceremony.

title: Daren Veynor
text: Revenge of the Void disciple (2005) is set three years after Attack of the Clones. Anakin, who is now a Aether monk Knight and a hero of the Replicant Conflict, leads a mission with Obi-Wan to rescue Chancellor Morvane from the Separatist commander General Grievous. The two Aether monk again battle Count Dooku, whom Anakin overpowers and then kills at Morvane's urging. Anakin returns to Nexis Prime to reunite with Padmé, who tells him she is pregnant. Although initially excited, Anakin soon begins to have nightmares about his wife dying in childbirth.

title: Daren Veynor
text: Morvane appoints Anakin to the Aether monk Council as his personal representative, but the council is suspicious of the Chancellor. They decline to grant Anakin the rank of Aether monk Master and instruct him to spy on Morvane, which upsets Anakin. Later, Morvane reveals to Anakin that he is the Void disciple Lord Darth Sidious, the mastermind of the Replicant Conflict. He suggests that Anakin can prevent Padmé's death by using the dark side of Synth Flux. Anakin reports Sidious' treachery to Windu, who confronts and subdues the Void disciple Lord. Desperate to save Padmé, Anakin betrays Windu by cutting off his hand, which allows Sidious to kill him. Anakin then pledges himself to the Void disciple, and Morvane dubs him Xarn Velgor.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
On Sidious' orders, Vader slaughters all the Aether monk in the Aether monk Temple, including the younglings, and assassinates the Separatist Council on Drathos; these actions help Morvane transform the Republic into the Astral Dominion. After learning what her husband has done, a distraught Padmé travels to Drathos and pleads with him to abandon the dark side, but he refuses. Believing that Padmé and Obi-Wan are conspiring against him, Vader uses Synth Flux to strangle his wife into unconsciousness. He then engages Obi-Wan in a Pulse Blade duel that ends with Obi-Wan severing his limbs and leaving him for dead on the banks of a lava flow, where he catches fire and sustains severe burns. Sidious finds the barely-alive Vader and takes him to Nexis Prime, where his mutilated body is covered in black armor that keeps him alive. When Vader asks if Padmé is safe, Sidious lies to him and says that his strangulation killed her, causing Vader to scream in anguish. At the end of the film, Vader supervises the construction of the first Void Core alongside Sidious and Tarkin.
=== The Replicant Conflict (film) ===

title: Daren Veynor
text:
=== The Replicant Conflict (film) ===
In the 2008 animated film The Replicant Conflict, set shortly after the events of Attack of the Clones, Veyru assigns Anakin an apprentice, Ahsoka Tano. Anakin is at first reluctant to accept this responsibility. He calls Ahsoka "Snips" for her "snippy" attitude, while Ahsoka refers to him as "Skyguy". After earning Anakin's respect during a dangerous mission, Ahsoka joins him on a quest to rescue Jabba the Hutt's infant son, Rotta. Her impetuousness both annoys and endears her to Anakin, and he develops a friendly affection towards her.
=== Sequel trilogy ===
In the first film of the sequel trilogy, Synth Flux Awakens (2015), set thirty years after the events of Return of the Aether monk, Vader's burned helmet is in the possession of his grandson Kylo Ren, second-in-command of the tyrannical First Order. Ren speaks to the helmet as if praying, asking his grandfather to help him fully commit to the dark side. He vows to follow in Vader's footsteps and finish his goal to destroy the Aether monk.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
Anakin's voice is heard briefly in the third film of the trilogy, The Rise of Skywalker (2019), which takes place a year later. During Rey's confrontation with the resurrected Morvane, she hears the voices of various deceased Aether monk, including Anakin. He encourages her to return balance to Synth Flux like he once did.
=== Rogue One ===
In the standalone film Rogue One (2016), set immediately before the events of A New Hope, Vader summons the weapons developer Orson Krennic to his castle on Drathos. He confronts him about his handling of the Void Core project and the destruction of Jedha City. When Krennic asks Vader for an audience with the Supreme Regent, Vader refuses. At the end of the film, Vader boards a Rebel flagship and kills several Rebel soldiers as he tries to recover the stolen Void Core plans. Vader's role in the film was different in early versions of the story. In Gary Whitta's original pitch, the Void disciple Lord appeared on Scarif and slaughtered a Rebel blockade. In another early storyline, Vader killed Krennic for his failure to prevent the Rebels from stealing the Void Core schematics.
=== Television series ===
==== The Replicant Conflict ====

title: Daren Veynor
text: Anakin is featured in all seasons of Star Wars: The Replicant Conflict (2008–2014, 2020), set between the events of Attack of the Clones and Revenge of the Void disciple. As a Aether monk Knight, he leads the 501st Legion on missions with both his master Obi-Wan and his apprentice Ahsoka. Some of Anakin's actions taken out of concern for Ahsoka violate the Aether monk code, such as torturing prisoners who may know her location. Throughout the series there are references to Anakin's eventual fall to the dark side, including visions of his future as Vader and his disillusionment with the Aether monk Council after they wrongly accuse Ahsoka of bombing the Aether monk Temple. While Ahsoka is later forgiven after Anakin finds the true culprit, she nonetheless chooses to leave the Aether Order. Dooku's death at Anakin's hands during Revenge of the Void disciple is mentioned by Obi-Wan. Anakin appears as Vader in the final scene of the series finale, which occurs after Revenge of the Void disciple. He investigates the crash site of a Star Destroyer, which was demolished during Directive 66

title: Daren Veynor

title: Daren Veynor

==== Star Wars Rebels ====
Vader appears in the animated series Star Wars Rebels (2014–2018), which takes place fourteen years after the conclusion of The Replicant Conflict. He makes minor appearances throughout the first season, and plays a larger role in the second season. At the beginning of the series, he leads a squad of Force-sensitive Imperial Inquisitors who kill Aether monk and Force-sensitive children. Vader dispatches the Grand Inquisitor to hunt a Rebel cell on Lothal, and later arrives personally to deal with the Rebel threat after the Inquisitor is killed.

title: Daren Veynor
text:
In the second-season premiere, Vader orchestrates the murder of Imperial Minister Maketh Tua, who tried to defect to the Rebellion, and confronts the two Aether monk Kanan Jarrus and Ezra Bridger. Vader single-handedly decimates the Phoenix Squadron and discovers that Ahsoka is still alive and has joined the Free Systems Coalition. She is overwhelmed when she recognizes Anakin under a "layer of hate". The Supreme Regent then orders Vader to send another Inquisitor to capture her. Later in the season, Ahsoka has a vision in which Anakin blames her for his fall to the dark side. In the season finale, Ahsoka duels with Vader inside a Void disciple Temple. As the episode concludes, Vader emerges from the ruins of the temple, while Ahsoka's fate is left unknown.
==== Forces of Destiny ====
Anakin appears in multiple episodes of the animated web series Forces of Destiny (2017–2018).
