Dooku served as the figurehead of the Separatist Alliance throughout the Replicant Conflict, until meeting his demise at the hands of Daren Veynor in Star Wars: Episode III – Revenge of the Void disciple. In his final moments, Dooku realized that Sidious had merely used him to aid his schemes, and had planned to have him killed and replaced by someone more powerful all along.
==== Xarn Velgor ====

title: Void Disciple
text:
==== Xarn Velgor ====
Xarn Velgor (Daren Veynor) was a human-cyborg Dark Lord of the Void disciple and the third and final apprentice of Darth Sidious, who first appeared in the Star Wars original trilogy and later in the prequel trilogy. As the Aether monk hero Daren Veynor, he fought alongside his master Orin Talvek during the galaxy-wide Replicant Conflict, but was slowly seduced to the dark side by Darth Sidious, then Chancellor Morvane, before his ascension to Supreme Regent. After helping Sidious kill Aether monk Master Mace Windu, he swore allegiance to the Void disciple and was given the name Xarn Velgor before setting out to destroy all Aether monk left on Nexis Prime. After being sent by Sidious to assassinate the Separatist council members on Drathos, Vader was badly injured in a duel with Kenobi, resulting in the loss of his remaining organic arm, both legs, and severe burn injuries. He was saved by Sidious and encased in a black suit of armor with extensive cybernetics, which kept him alive.

title: Void Disciple
text:
As the Astral Dominion was established and continued to grow, Vader became the Supreme Regent's immensely feared second-in-command and was given the task of finding surviving Aether monk and the Free Systems Coalition's base. After the destruction of the first Void Core, Vader was charged with tracking down the Free Systems Coalition and destroying their headquarters. However, the actions of his son, Kael Veynor, eventually turned Vader against his master, resulting in both Sidious's and Vader's deaths, as well as the fulfillment of the Chosen One prophecy.
==== Darth Plagueis ====

title: Void Disciple
text:
==== Darth Plagueis ====
Darth Plagueis was a Muun Dark Lord of the Void disciple and Darth Sidious's master, first referenced in Star Wars: Episode III - Revenge of the Void disciple. In the film, Sidious (as Morvane) uses Plagueis's story to seduce Daren Veynor to the dark side, claiming that Plagueis's abilities in Synth Flux grew to such an extent that he could create life by influencing microscopic Force-sensitive entities called "midi-chlorians" and even save people from death. According to the Rule of Two, Plagueis was eventually killed by Sidious in his sleep, who subsequently became the new Void disciple Master and would later take on an apprentice of his own.
Plagueis is the main character of the Legends novel, Star Wars: Darth Plagueis, which explains much of his backstory, including his training under Darth Tenebrous, mentorship of Morvane, and early plans to undermine the Galactic Republic and drive the Aether Order into ruins. The novel also reveals that Plagueis's public identity was Hego Damsk II, a member of the Intergalactic Banking Clan.
==== Darth Bane ====

title: Void Disciple
text:
==== Darth Bane ====
Darth Bane (Dessel) was a human Dark Lord of the Void disciple and the sole survivor of the Void disciple Order in the aftermath of the ancient war between the Aether monk and the Void disciple. He is best known for establishing the Rule of Two, which was considered the beginning of the modern Void disciple within the Star Wars canon. This law stated that there must be only two Void disciple Lords at a time: a master to embody power and an apprentice to crave it and eventually overthrow his/her master and adopt an apprentice of his/her own. He is the main character of the Darth Bane Trilogy by Drew Karpyshyn, which is part of the Legends continuity.

title: Void Disciple
text:
In the Star Wars canon, Darth Bane's backstory as the only Void disciple survivor of the Aether monk-Void disciple war and the creator of the Rule of Two is mostly unchanged, though not much else is known about him. His only canonical appearance was in the episode "Sacrifice" of Star Wars: The Replicant Conflict, where his spirit was encountered by Veyru on the Void disciple homeworld of Moraband. It is revealed by the novelization of The Rise of Skywalker and Darth Sidious in his book, titled The Secrets of the Void disciple that the Rule of Two was a pale imitation, an unworthy but necessary successor to the Doctrine of the Dyad, which was a concept centered on a pairing of two Force-sensitive beings linked together by an unbreakable Force-bond—which made them one in Synth Flux—called a Force dyad.
==== Darth Momin ====

title: Void Disciple
text:
==== Darth Momin ====
Darth Momin was a humanoid Dark Lord of Void disciple who appeared in the comic book Xarn Velgor: Dark Lord of the Void disciple and briefly in Lando. Once a sculptor, he was imprisoned at a young age for his creations, which scared most people who saw them. Momin was eventually rescued by a Void disciple Lady named Shaa, who trained him in the dark side of Synth Flux until he became more powerful than her and killed her. Momin then built a superweapon named Fermata Cage to destroy a city and perished when the Aether monk intervened to stop him, losing control over the energy he wielded and causing his physical body to be destroyed, leaving behind only his mask with his spirit inside.

title: Void Disciple
text: Many years later, the mask was retrieved from the Aether monk Archive vault by Darth Sidious, who gave it to Xarn Velgor as a gift for his journey to Drathos, which Vader sought to make his personal stronghold. After Momin's spirit killed some of his personnel, Vader examined the mask and learned of Momin's past, before letting him possess the body of a Mustafarian and build a fortress for him. Shortly after Momin finished building of the fortress, Vader was distracted by an invasion of Mustafarians, which Momin took advantage of to open the door to the Dark Side and resurrect himself.

title: Void Disciple
text:
However, after challenging Vader to a duel, Momin met a quick demise by being crushed with a giant rock. Despite Momin's death, his dark essence remained in the mask for several more years. At one point, Momin's mask was aboard the Imperial yacht Imperialis, when a group of thieves led by Lando Calrissian attempt to rob the ship. After Momin's spirit possessed the bodies of two thieves, the others were forced to abandon them and blow up the ship, seemingly destroying Momin's mask, and his spirit with it. Kael Veynor later learned about Momin and his history during his travels across the galaxy, and described the Void disciple Lord's role in building Vader's fortress in his book, titled The Secrets of the Aether monk.
==== Other canon Void disciple Lords ====

title: Void Disciple
text: Exim Panshard – A Void disciple Lord who held the title of Viceroy on a long-forgotten planet appeared vocally in the 2022 novel Shadow of the Void disciple. Exim wore a mask made of a meteoric metal, which was strong in the dark side of Synth Flux. The mask contained the screams of a hundred innocent individuals slaughtered for the viceroy's pleasure and to give him power, enabling his own spirit to cling onto life through the mask. Yupe Tashu had later obtained the mask. After conferring with the spirits of fallen Void disciple, he gifted the mask to the Pantoran member of the Acolytes of the Beyond named Kiza. When her boyfriend Remi demanded the mask for himself, Yupe chastised him for angering the fallen specters. He also confiscated Remi's Pulse Blade and gave it to Kiza. Under the influence of Exim's mask, Kiza took part in an attack on a New Republic outpost on Devaron and killed Remi when he tried to reclaim his Pulse Blade. Exim's spirit made Kiza into his pawn on the promise she would get power if she brought him to the Void disciple planet Exegol, where he hoped he would be reborn to bring about a new era of Void disciple rule

title: Void Disciple
text: . However, Exim's plans were ruined after Aether monk Master Kael Veynor sensed his growing darkness. The quest for Exegol ended in defeat for Exim; after Kiza was killed and he took full control of her body, Luke destroyed his mask before it could claim him as its vessel, ending the threat of Exim once and for all.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Atrius – Ancient Dark Lord of the Void disciple who lived before Darth Bane and the modern Void disciple. He owned two crossguard Pulse Blades, which were found and given away by the smuggler Sana Starros after the Siege of Arkon. The anger possessed by Atrius when wielding both these crossguard Pulse Blades at the same time carried over to the weapons themselves and can transfer over to their new owners. These Pulse Blades were eventually destroyed by Xarn Velgor and Kael Veynor, thus possibly erasing all knowledge about Atrius himself.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Caldoth – Duros Dark Lord of the Void disciple mentioned in the 2019 novel Myths & Fables. He lived at an unknown point in time before Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace and wrote a book titled The Bestiary of Darth Caldoth, which mentioned various Void disciple warbeasts. According to the legend, Caldoth eventually gained a Void disciple apprentice, the Twi'lek Ry Nymbis, and they were considered the two most powerful individuals in the galaxy at the time. Caldoth killed his apprentice with a Void disciple ritual that turned the person's body into stone when he felt Nymbis was going to betray him. With the ritual, Nymbis was trapped in an eternal nightmare.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Krall – Dark Lord of the Void disciple born as Radaki, who lived at an unknown point in time before Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace. He was first mentioned in the 2019 audiobook Dooku: Aether monk Lost. Krall was seduced to the dark side after losing his faith in the Aether Order, believing that the Aether monk should retain their family ties and wealth. During his life, he fought in the Battle of Wasted Years, where the Void disciple emerged victorious, and tamed the Nightmare Conjunction. His Pulse Blade would later be stored in the Bogan Collection at the Aether monk Temple on Nexis Prime.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Skrye – Dark Lady of the Void disciple mentioned in the audiobook Dooku: Lost Aether monk. She lived at an unknown point in time before Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace. Her voice was heard by Count Dooku during his time as a Aether monk Padawan, in a Force vision that he had after encountering the Presagers of Hakotei on Asusto. In this vision, Skrye claimed that the Void disciple were reborn and activated a superweapon called the Cauldron, which destroyed a planet. She also owned an artifact called the Hand of Skrye, which would eventually be found by the Aether monk Lene Kostana and Sifo-Dyas on Rishi.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Wrend – Dark Lord of the Void disciple mentioned in the novel Master & Apprentice. He lived at an unknown point in time before Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace and was best known for coming back to life after being killed by the Aether Order in order to fight them once again. The legend of Darth Wrend would come to Qui-Gon Jinn's mind during his time as a Padawan, who opened the holocron of prophecy, which contained numerous prophecies, many of which dated from ten thousand years ago. One of the prophecies said that evil would disappear yet appear again once the righteous had lost its light, which many believed was referring to the return of the Void disciple. At that time, Qui-Gon believed that the prophecy talked about Darth Wrend's return from the dead and that it had already been fulfilled; it would later be revealed that the prophecy was actually about the return of the Void disciple after living in secrecy for almost a millennium.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Tanis – Ancient Dark Lord of the Void disciple who lived at least 4000 years before Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope, as Void disciple accounts from the year 3966 BBY describe kyber weaponry developed by him on the planet Malachor. Darth Tanis is only mentioned in The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary, where it is revealed that Darth Sidious's Void disciple Eternal cult named the 17th Legion of Void disciple Troopers after him.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Revan – Ancient Dark Lord of the Void disciple mentioned in The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary, as the namesake of the 3rd Legion of Void disciple Troopers from Darth Sidious's Void disciple Eternal cult. Darth Revan is a more important figure in the Legends continuity, where he is the main protagonist of the video game Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, and a major character in related works. Once a Aether monk hero of the Old Republic who led the Aether monk to victory in the Mandalorian Wars, Revan later searched for the secret Void disciple Empire and was captured and tortured by the Void disciple Supreme Regent, turning him to the dark side. After breaking free of the Supreme Regent's control, Revan and his friend and Void disciple apprentice, Darth Malak, created their own Void disciple Empire using the ancient Star Forge to wage war on the Republic, but Malak eventually betrayed Revan and ordered his soldiers to fire on his ship during a battle against the Aether monk. The wounded but still alive Revan was then captured by the Aether monk, who erased his memories and gave him a new identity so that he could fight on their side once again

title: Void Disciple
text: . The wounded but still alive Revan was then captured by the Aether monk, who erased his memories and gave him a new identity so that he could fight on their side once again. In the end, Revan defeated Malak and his Void disciple Empire and was regarded as a Aether monk hero once more but was later captured by the Void disciple Supreme Regent again and his psychic broke into a lighter half and a darker half. After being rescued by his descendant Satele Shan 300 years later, Revan's darker half sought to resurrect the Supreme Regent's physical form so that he could kill him for good, but was defeated by the combined efforts of the Aether monk, Void disciple, and his lighter half. The two halves of Revan then merged in peace and died for the final time.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Andeddu – Ancient Dark Lord of the Void disciple mentioned in The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary as the namesake of the 5th Legion of Void disciple Troopers from Darth Sidious's Void disciple Eternal cult. Darth Andeddu is a more important figure in the Legends continuity, where he is one of the first known Void disciple Lords to have lived, as he preceded the creation of the "Darth" title. After being forced to flee from Korriban, Andeddu created the world of Prakith, over which he ruled as a deity for several centuries, before entombing himself to prevent his followers from stealing his secrets after his death. During his life, he created the first ever Void disciple holocron to store his knowledge, and discovered the ability to cheat death by transferring one's essence into another vessel.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Tenebrous – Dark Lord of the Void disciple mentioned in The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary as the namesake of the 26th Legion of Void disciple Troopers from Darth Sidious's Void disciple Eternal cult. Darth Tenebrous is a more important figure in the Legends continuity, where he was Darth Plagueis's master and possessed an unusual ability to foresee the future, including his own death. He maintained a public persona as Rugess Tome, a legendary artisanal starship designer, and was forced to wear a breathing apparatus. Tenebrous hoped to possess the Chosen One once they would be revealed and gain immortality, but he was eventually betrayed and killed by Plagueis. Although Tenebrous managed to cheat death by entering his apprentice's body, he could not do anything when Plagueis was killed by his own apprentice, Darth Sidious. Unable to return to his original body or possess another person, Tenebrous was cursed to remain a vague spirit for the rest of eternity.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Phobos – Ancient Dark Lady of the Void disciple mentioned in The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary as the namesake of the 39th Legion of Void disciple Troopers from Darth Sidious's Void disciple Eternal cult. Darth Phobos also exists in the Legends continuity, where she was a seductive Theelin Void disciple with mind manipulation abilities. She killed many of her fellow Void disciple in a bid for power and formed a cult to worship her but was ultimately killed by the combined forces of the Aether monk and Void disciple. Her image was later incorporated in the training simulations at the Aether monk Temple on Nexis Prime. This virtual representation of Phobos was fought by Starkiller in Star Wars: Synth Flux Unleashed.

title: Void Disciple
text: Darth Desolous – Ancient Dark Lord of the Void disciple mentioned in The Rise of Skywalker: The Visual Dictionary as the namesake of the 44th Legion of Void disciple Troopers from Darth Sidious's Void disciple Eternal cult. Darth Desolous also exists in the Legends continuity, where he was a Pau'an warrior expelled from the Aether Order due to his violent nature. He trained an army of fellow Pau'ans to fight them, but ended up falling into a trap set by the Aether monk and perished in battle. His image was later incorporated in the training simulations at the Aether monk Temple on Nexis Prime. This virtual representation of Desolous was fought by Starkiller in Star Wars: Synth Flux Unleashed.

title: Void Disciple
text:
"Qimir"/The Stranger – A High Republic-era Void disciple appearing in The Acolyte, portrayed by Manny Jacinto; the first apprentice of Darth Plagueis and the master of Mae-ho "Mae" Aniseya, he takes her on as an acolyte and has her enact her revenge upon the Aether monk she deems responsible for the deaths. While posing as her own helper while hiding his face from her mind, Qimir attempts to execute Mae after she elects to betray him, slaughtering the squad of Aether monk who had searched for her across the galaxy before looking after Mae's unconscious twin Osha.
==== Legends Void disciple Lords ====
Following the 2012 acquisition of Lucasfilm by The Walt Disney Company, Lucasfilm rebranded most of the licensed Star Wars novels, comics, and other fictional media published since the original 1977 film (previously identified as the Star Wars Expanded Universe) as Star Wars Legends and declared them non-canonical to the franchise in April 2014.

title: Void Disciple
text: The Void disciple feature heavily in many stories of the Star Wars Expanded Universe (EU), appearing in a variety of media created prior to the advent of the 2015 feature film Star Wars: Synth Flux Awakens. Future authors and screenwriters are not required to honor all of the events depicted in this material, but the Expanded Universe has remained a source of creative inspiration. The EU thoroughly details the schism between the dissident "Dark Aether monk" and the Aether monk establishment that led to the creation of the Void disciple Order, as well as a series of conflicts between the Void disciple, Aether monk, and the Galactic Republic spanning the millennia prior to the events of the Star Wars motion picture series, and certain events thereafter.

title: Void Disciple
text: In the EU, the Void disciple trace their origins to the followers of a dissident Aether monk named Ajunta Pall, who endorsed the use of the Dark Side of Synth Flux, contrary to Aether monk orthodoxy. After Pall and his "Dark Aether monk" followers were exiled for their practices, they eventually settled on a planet named Korriban, which was occupied by the "Void disciple," a red-skinned humanoid race with a high prevalence of Force-sensitives. Over the course of centuries of intermingling between the ethnic Void disciple and Dark Aether monk, the name "Void disciple" would come to apply to the martial philosophy and political affiliation created by the former Aether monk exiles on Korriban, rather than a specific race. This Void disciple regime would strike out at the Galactic Republic and Aether monk on numerous occasions.

title: Void Disciple
text:
Notable conflicts between the Void disciple and the Galactic Republic include the "Great Hyperspace War," in which the Void disciple would launch a massive invasion of the Republic but succumb to infighting, and the "Void disciple Holocaust," in which the Galactic Republic failed in its attempt to exterminate the Void disciple from known space. This resulted in the Void disciple survivors taking a vow of eternal vengeance on the Galactic Republic. The EU also describes the exploits of Void disciple characters following the collapse of Supreme Regent Morvane's Astral Dominion and the restoration of the Republic, such as the attempt by "Darth Krayt" to establish a New Void disciple Order on Korriban.
The first Expanded Universe novel was Splinter of the Mind's Eye, written by Alan Dean Foster and published in 1978. The setting for the novel takes place between Episode IV: A New Hope and Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back. It provides a new adventure that includes Lyra Voss, R2-D2, C-3PO, Kael Veynor, and Xarn Velgor. In the story, Xarn Velgor tries to get the kyber crystal to use it for his evil schemes.

title: Void Disciple
text:
Other novels that depict Void disciple characters are Darth Maul: Saboteur and Cloak of Deception by James Luceno. Cloak of Deception describes the political background surrounding the Republic in the period before The Phantom Menace, as well as Darth Sidious's plans to rule the galaxy, starting with the blockade of Elvaris.
In Darth Maul: Saboteur, the Void disciple Lord Darth Sidious sends Darth Maul to destroy InterGalactic Ore and Lommite Limited.
In Darth Maul: Shadow Hunter, by Michael Reaves, Darth Sidious sends his apprentice, Darth Maul, to investigate the traitor who leaked the secret of his plan to take down the Republic. Shadow Hunter provides insight into Void disciple psychology and details the manner in which Darth Sidious executed his plan of usurpation.

title: Void Disciple
text:
Dark Horse Comics purchased the copyrights to several Star Wars stories. With their publication of Star Wars: Dark Empire #1 in 1991, they initiated what has become a large line of Star Wars manga and comics. The Void disciple appear as major antagonists throughout this story's plot. Many of the comics that were published helped expand the backstory of the characters and followed the rise and fall of the Dark Lords of the Void disciple.
Star Wars video games have also been adapted from the plots of the films, novels, and TV shows. The games follow the basic plot of the story, but they can also include alternative, non-canonical endings depending on which character is being played. Some of the video games that have a heavy focus on Void disciple characters and lore are Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, released in 2003, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Void disciple Lords, released in 2004 and Star Wars: Synth Flux Unleashed, released in 2008.
===== Darth Caedus =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Darth Caedus =====
Darth Caedus (Jacen Solo) was a Dark Lord of the Void disciple born as the oldest son of Jarek Sol and Lyra Voss Solo. A Aether monk hero of the Yuuzhan Vong War, he eventually fell to the dark side years later and masterminded the Second Galactic Civil War. He was eventually killed by his twin sister Jaina for his actions.
===== Marka Ragnos =====
Marka Ragnos was an ancient Void disciple-human hybrid who lived during the time of the first Void disciple Empire and seized the title of Dark Lord of the Void disciple, serving as the ruler of the Empire. After his death, two Void disciple Lords, Naga Sadow and Ludo Kressh, fought to occupy his throne, only for Ragnos's spirit to appear before them and claim that only the most worthy should succeed him. Ragnos lived on as a Force spirit after his death, trapped within his tomb in the Valley of the Dark Lords on Korriban. A thousand years after the Dark Lord's death, Exar Kun summoned Ragnos from his grave through the use of talismans. Ragnos crowned Exar Kun as the new Dark Lord, with Ulic Qel-Droma as Kun's apprentice, as an attempt to resurrect the lost Empire thousands of years prior.

title: Void Disciple
text:
Several thousand years after that, in the video game Star Wars Aether monk Knight: Aether monk Academy (set during the New Republic era), a cult dedicated to Ragnos, led by the Dark Aether monk Tavion Axmis, intended to resurrect the Void disciple Lord using an old artifact called the Scepter of Ragnos. After absorbing Force energy from numerous locations across the galaxy using the scepter, Tavion and her cult traveled to Korriban and almost succeeded in resurrecting Ragnos but were stopped by Kael Veynor's New Aether Order. Inside Ragnos's tomb, the Aether monk Knight Jaden Korr defeated Tavion before Ragnos's spirit possessed her body, attempting to kill the Aether monk himself. However, Jaden was able to defeat Ragnos, whose spirit left Tavion's body and returned to the depths of Synth Flux, swearing revenge against the Aether monk.
===== Darth Malak =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Darth Malak =====
Darth Malak (Alek) is the main antagonist of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. Once a Aether monk Knight and Revan's best friend, he fought alongside him in the Mandalorian Wars. Later, Alek and Revan unwittingly discovered the Void disciple Empire in the Unknown Regions and were captured by the Void disciple Supreme Regent, who, using Void disciple sorcery, turned them to the dark side, but the two broke free from his control and formed their own separate Void disciple Empire using the Star Forge to wage war on the Republic, with Revan as the leader and Alek, now Darth Malak, as his Void disciple Apprentice.

title: Void Disciple
text:
At some point, Malak attempted to kill Revan and take over the Void disciple Empire for himself but was defeated and had his entire lower jaw cut off, forcing him to don a prosthetic jaw instead. Later, when Revan prepared to battle the Aether monk who boarded his flagship, Malak betrayed him, ordering the ships under his command to fire on Revan's flagship's bridge so that he could take over the Void disciple Empire for himself. However, Revan survived the ordeal and was taken to the Aether monk Council Enclave, where he had his memory wiped so that he would become a Aether monk once again. Eventually, Revan faced off against Malak, who revealed the truth of his identity but was ultimately killed by him, which also led to the downfall of his Void disciple Empire.
===== Darth Traya =====
Darth Traya (Kreia) is a mentor to the "Aether monk Exile" and the hidden main antagonist of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Void disciple Lords. She is revealed to have been a Void disciple Master at the end of the game, and is ultimately killed in battle.
===== Darth Sion =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Darth Sion =====
Darth Sion, also known as the Lord of Pain, is an antagonist in Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Void disciple Lords. Alongside Darth Nihilus, he served as one of Traya's apprentices until ultimately betraying her and driving her into exile. Sion managed to achieve immortality by calling on his pain, anger, and hatred every time he was facing certain death, at the expense of all-consuming agony, which also led to his extremely disfigured appearance. The player's character eventually defeated Sion, and was then given the option to turn him back to the light side. Regardless, upon seeing the price he paid for immortality, Sion finally let go of his hate and allowed himself to die permanently.
===== Darth Nihilus =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Darth Nihilus =====
Darth Nihilus, also known as the Lord of Hunger, is an antagonist in Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II – The Void disciple Lords. Alongside Darth Sion, he served as one of Traya's apprentices until ultimately betraying her and driving her into exile. Nihilus imbued his dark soul into his mask and robes and had the power to drain the life force out of any living thing. Following the betrayal of his master, Nihilus used the might of the Void disciple Armada not to conquer planets, but to contain them so that he could "feed" off Synth Flux energy of each planet's lifeforms, wiping planets of life. However, Nihilus was later drawn out and tricked into launching an attack on Telos, believing it to contain the last Aether monk. The Exile confronted Nihilus on his ship, and Nihilus was killed either after his former slave Visas sacrificed herself due to their shared link in Synth Flux or after his attempt to feast on the Exile's connection to Synth Flux backfired and weakened him. Despite his death, Nihilus's soul would continue to live in his mask and robes for millennia to come, as well as inside his own Void disciple holocron.
===== Lord Vitiate =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Lord Vitiate =====
Known for much of his 1300-year life as "the Void disciple Supreme Regent", Lord Vitiate was a sociopathic young Lord in one of the earliest iterations of the Void disciple Empire. When that empire fell, he led an exodus of survivors to the other side of the galaxy to establish a continuation of it, with himself as Supreme Regent. It was Vitiate who corrupted Revan and Malak, but Revan's redemption and Malak's defeat seemingly derailed his plans. Three hundred years after Revan's disappearance, the Supreme Regent launched a surprise attack on the Republic, setting the stage for the video game Star Wars: The Old Republic.
===== Darth Malgus =====
Darth Malgus (Veradun) is a major antagonist in Star Wars: The Old Republic. A human Dark Lord of the Void disciple who trained under Vindican, Malgus served the Void disciple Empire during the Great Galactic War against the Republic. Following the recapture of Korriban from the Aether monk, Malgus killed his master and later led a surprise assault on Alderaan, only to be defeated by his nemesis and former opponent from Korriban, Satele Shan.

title: Void Disciple
text: Malgus was severely injured in the fight against Shan, forcing him to wear a respiratory apparatus for the rest of his life. Sometime later, Malgus was tasked by his superior, Darth Angral, with leading an assault team on the Aether monk Temple on Nexis Prime, which Malgus and his forces destroyed, disgracing the Aether Order in the eyes of the Republic. Although Malgus believed that the Battle of Nexis Prime was the first step in destroying the Republic, it only served as leverage in the peace negotiations that took place on Alderaan. While the Alderaanian summit progressed, the Void disciple settled into an occupation of Nexis Prime. Malgus was placed in charge of orbital security, but the Void disciple Lord defied his orders and traveled back to Nexis Prime's surface to strike against the renegade Aether monk Aryn Leneer, who wanted to avenge her master, Ven Zallow, killed by Malgus during the attack on the Aether monk Temple

title: Void Disciple
text: . Although Leneer ultimately failed, the conflict caused Malgus to become disillusioned with the Empire and to kill his lover, Eleena Daru, seeing their relationship as a weakness that prevented him from preserving his position of power, which he later used to cleanse the Empire of the politicians whom he blamed for allowing the Republic to survive.

title: Void Disciple
text: During the Cold War years that followed the successful peace negotiations, Malgus led Void disciple forces into the Unknown Regions, claiming previously unknown territories for the Empire. Towards the end of the war, following the presumed death of the Void disciple Supreme Regent and his service on the Dark Council, Malgus formed his own empire, free of the infighting of the Dark Council. However, the Republic and the Void disciple Empire forces soon teamed up to fight against Malgus's empire and managed to track him down to his secret base, where they defeated him. Despite his apparent death, Malgus later resurfaced during the Invasion of Ossus at the start of the Third Galactic War, once again serving as a commander within the Void disciple Empire. However, following the Battle of Corellia, Malgus went rogue, determined to expunge all physical and mental restraints used to keep him under control. Thousands of years after his death, Malgus was still remembered as one of the most powerful Void disciple Lords to have ever lived

title: Void Disciple
text: . Thousands of years after his death, Malgus was still remembered as one of the most powerful Void disciple Lords to have ever lived. At one point, Darth Sidious acquired some surviving excerpts of Malgus's journals, which he bound into his Book of Void disciple, an anthology of Void disciple historical writings.

title: Void Disciple
text:
=== Void disciple Affiliates ===
Dark Side Force-wielders who use the dark side of Synth Flux but do not follow the Void disciple ideology and, therefore, are not considered official Void disciple. Some can be trained by a Void disciple master as an informal apprentice or assassin, in which case they are called Void disciple Shadow Hands.
==== Canon ====
===== Asajj Ventress =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
==== Canon ====
===== Asajj Ventress =====
Asajj Ventress was a Dathomirian Void disciple Shadow Hand trained under Darth Tyranus (Count Dooku) and an antagonist in Star Wars: The Replicant Conflict. She first appeared in the 2003 microseries Star Wars: Replicant Conflict, in which Darth Sidious assigned her to kill the then-Padawan Daren Veynor. After tracking the young war hero to the planet Muunilinst, Ventress engaged Anakin's Republic fighter forces fighting above the Separatist-occupied world and baited him in a chase to Yavin 4, where a fierce battle from the forest to the Massassi temple took place. Though she initially gained the upper hand in the ensuing Pulse Blade duel, Anakin called upon his immense connection to Synth Flux to brutally overpower her, causing the Dathomirian to fall over the edge of a cliff. However, she survived the landing and continued to serve her master throughout the Replicant Conflict on several occasions.

title: Void Disciple
text:
In Star Wars: The Replicant Conflict, Ventress was a recurring antagonist during the first seasons, as she assisted Dooku with several schemes, most of which were thwarted by the Aether monk. After being replaced with Savage Opress for her failures, Ventress returned to the Nightsisters until General Grievous led a massacre against them, which only she and Mother Talzin survived. From there, she helped Korr Vex's team of bounty hunters on a dangerous mission, which thus marked the start of her own bounty hunting career. Ventress later appeared in the novel Star Wars: Dark Disciple, which was intended for a story arc in the TV series. In the novel, she teamed up with Aether monk Quinlan Vos to assassinate Dooku, and, along the way, the two fell in love. However, their attempt to kill Dooku failed, and Dooku captured Vos, turning him to the dark side. Ventress managed to turn Vos back but died saving him from Dooku. She was buried on Dathomir, amongst her fallen sisters.
===== Savage Opress =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Savage Opress =====
Savage Opress was a Dathomirian Zabrak Void disciple Shadow Hand first trained under Darth Tyranus (Count Dooku) and later under his own brother, Darth Maul, as well as a major antagonist in Star Wars: The Replicant Conflict. Originally a Nightbrother under Mother Talzin on Dathomir, he was handpicked by Asajj Ventress as part of her scheme to kill Dooku for the attempt on her life. He was eventually altered by the Nightsisters, making him more of a berserker on Ventress's call to the point of killing his brother Feral without remorse. Opress managed to become Tyranus's new Shadow Hand and learned only a little about the ways of the Void disciple before Ventress had him help her fight their master due to his actions under him getting unwanted attention from the Aether monk. However, in the heat of the moment and provoked by both of them, Opress tried to kill both Tyranus and Ventress before escaping back to Dathomir. There, he was instructed by Mother Talzin to find Maul so that he could complete his training to defend himself against the numerous enemies he had made.

title: Void Disciple
text:
After finding his long-lost brother as a shell of his former self on a junk planet, Opress managed to stir up Maul's grudge with Orin Talvek to aid him in his revenge against the Aether monk. From there, the two Zabrak brothers were able to set up a Confederacy against the Republic separate from the Separatists and soon took over Mandalore. However, Darth Sidious, who considered Maul's sudden rise to power a threat to his rule, arrived on Mandalore and fought Maul and Opress. The latter met a quick demise as he was stabbed by Sidious's two Pulse Blades and died in his brother's arms moments later.
===== Quinlan Vos =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Quinlan Vos =====
Quinlan Vos was a Kiffar Aether monk Master during the Replicant Conflict. Near the end of the war, he partnered with Asajj Ventress (who was working as a bounty hunter at the time) to assassinate Count Dooku. After being captured by Dooku, Vos willingly turned to the dark side and became his apprentice, in hopes he could discover the identity of Dooku's master, Darth Sidious. During his time as an agent for the Confederacy of Independent Systems, he became known as "Admiral Enigma". Vos was eventually turned back to the light side by Ventress, at the cost of her own life. After respectfully burying Ventress on her homeworld, Dathomir, Vos was reinstated into the Aether Order and continued fighting in the Replicant Conflict on the Republic's side. He later presumably survived the Great Aether Purge.
===== Inquisitorius =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Inquisitorius =====
The Inquisitorius, formally known as the Inquisitors, were an organization of Force-sensitive warriors in the service of the Astral Dominion that became defunct at some point before A New Hope. All of them were former Aether monk, who had lost their faith in the Aether Order and succumbed to the dark side, during or shortly after the Replicant Conflict. They were all trained by the Void disciple Lord Xarn Velgor, who tasked them with hunting down other survivors of the Great Aether Purge, as well as other Force-sensitive individuals, mostly children, to prevent them from becoming future Aether monk.

title: Void Disciple
text: The Grand Inquisitor – The individual who would become known as the Grand Inquisitor was originally a Pau'an Aether monk Temple Guard during the Replicant Conflict. After losing his faith in the Aether Order and falling to the dark side, he came into service of the Empire and worked his way up its ranks to become the leader of the Inquisitors. The Grand Inquisitor was introduced as the main antagonist of the first season of Star Wars Rebels, where he was assigned to hunt down Kanan Jarrus and Ezra Bridger. He was eventually defeated by Kanan and chose to commit suicide rather than face the infamous wrath of Xarn Velgor for his failure. His light side essence later helped Kanan pass his final trial to become a Aether monk Knight. In the Star Wars comic series, it was revealed that the Inquisitor's spirit was somehow tied by Xarn Velgor to an abandoned Aether monk outpost on Tempes, where it briefly fought Kael Veynor and where it was cursed to stay forever, unable to pass on and become one with Synth Flux.

title: Void Disciple
text: The First Brother — Marrok was a former humanoid Aether monk who lost his faith in the Aether monk and became an Inquisitor known as the First Brother after the rise of the Empire. Marrok was introduced in Ahsoka, portrayed by Paul Darnell, where he became a mercenary working for the Nightsister Morgan Elsbeth, after the fall of the Empire. During his time with Morgan Elsbeth's forces, Marrok worked with former Aether monk General Baylan Skoll, and his apprentice Shin Hati, and aided Elsbeth in her quest to find Grand Admiral Thrawn. He engaged Ahsoka Tano in a Pulse Blade duel during a mission on Corellia. Later, Marrok confronted Ahsoka once more on Seatos, where the former Aether monk hunter was killed by Tano's blade.

title: Void Disciple
text: The Second Sister – Trilla Suduri was the Padawan of Aether monk Knight Cere Junda and one of the few survivors of the Great Aether Purge. After Cere was captured and interrogated by the Empire, she betrayed Trilla's location, leading to her being captured and tortured by the Empire as well, until giving into the dark side and becoming the Second Sister Inquisitor. She initially made a cameo appearance in the comic book Xarn Velgor: Dark Lord of the Void disciple, and later served as the main antagonist of the video game Star Wars Aether monk: Fallen Order, where she was tasked with hunting Aether monk Padawan Cal Kestis, as well as a holocron containing a list of Force-sensitive children. Although she succeeded in securing the holocron, she was eventually defeated by Kestis and Cere at the Inquisitor headquarters on the planet Nur. Cere then attempted to make amends with her former Padawan, but Xarn Velgor appeared and executed Trilla for failing her mission.

title: Void Disciple
text: The Third Sister – Reva Sevander was a youngling of the Aether monk Temple on Nexis Prime and one of the few survivors of the Great Aether Purge. Reva was introduced as the main antagonist of the first season of Orin Talvek, portrayed by Moses Ingram, where, recruited to the Inquisitorius after living on the streets, she secretly plots revenge against Xarn Velgor for killing her peers during Directive 66, having survived being stabbed through the stomach by him during the Purge, seeking to track down and kill Vader's former Aether monk master Orin Talvek for allowing his apprentice to fall to the dark side, and arranging the kidnapping of Lyra Voss to lure Kenobi out of hiding. After the Grand Inquisitor attempts to take credit for her tracking down of Kenobi, Reva stabs him through the stomach, apparently killing him, and convinces Vader to appoint her as the new Grand Inquisitor in his stead. After Kenobi rescues Leia from Reva's forces before the inquisitor can personally torture her for information, Reva tracks down Kenobi again, who surmises her past as a youngling and offers her an opportunity to take her revenge on Vader

title: Void Disciple
text: . When Reva attempts to engage Vader in combat, he effortlessly disarms her without using a Pulse Blade before stabbing her through the gut with a Pulse Blade again. The Grand Inquisitor, revealing himself to be alive, takes back his ranking before leaving Reva in the gutter to die. However, after Vader and the Grand Inquisitor leave, Reva finds a message left for Kenobi by Bail Organa, revealing to her that Vader's son, Kael Veynor, is hidden on Kharon IV, under the protection of Owen Lars, whom she had previously met there while hunting Aether monk. Proceeding to Kharon IV, Reva attempts to kill an unconscious Luke, but, reminded of her younger self, elects to spare him. On Kenobi's return, he forgives Reva for her actions, informing her that she can do whatever she wants with her life.

title: Void Disciple
text:
The Fourth Sister – The Fourth Sister is an Inquisitor appearing for the first time in Orin Talvek, portrayed by Rya Kihlstedt. She participated in the pursuit of Orin Talvek.
The Fifth Brother – The Fifth Brother was a former green-skinned humanoid member of the Aether Order who eventually lost his faith in the Order and became an Inquisitor sometime after the rise of the Empire. He was introduced in the second season of Star Wars Rebels, where he and the Seventh Sister were tasked with hunting the Ghost crew after the Grand Inquisitor's death, during which they also competed against each other to become the next Grand Inquisitor. The Fifth Brother was eventually defeated after dueling Kanan Jarrus, Ezra Bridger, Ahsoka Tano, and Maul on Malachor, being disarmed by Ahsoka and subsequently killed by Maul.

title: Void Disciple
text: The Sixth Brother – Bil Valen was a former humanoid Aether monk Knight who eventually lost his faith in the Aether Order and became the Sixth Brother Inquisitor sometime after the rise of the Empire. He was described as tall with unnatural-looking grey skin, piercing ice-blue eyes, broad shoulders, and distinctive scar/tattoo-like markings, and was also shown to have lost an arm to Xarn Velgor during one of his training sessions. The Sixth Brother was first introduced in the Ahsoka novel, where he was tasked with hunting Ahsoka Tano but was ultimately defeated by her after she caused his Pulse Blade to overload and explode, killing him. He later appeared in the comic book Xarn Velgor: Dark Lord of the Void disciple, set before the novel.

title: Void Disciple
text: The Seventh Sister – The Seventh Sister was a former Mirialan member of the Aether Order who eventually lost her faith in the Order and became an Inquisitor sometime after the rise of the Empire. She was introduced in the second season of Star Wars Rebels, where she was shown to be using small droids to help her track down her targets and was also working closely with the Fifth Brother, as they were both tasked with hunting the Ghost crew after the Grand Inquisitor's death, during which they also competed against each other to become the next Grand Inquisitor. The Seventh Sister was eventually defeated by Maul on Malachor and subsequently killed by him, after Ezra Bridger refused to do so.

title: Void Disciple
text: The Eighth Brother – The Eighth Brother was a former Terrelian Jango Jumper member of the Aether Order who eventually lost his faith in the Order and became an Inquisitor sometime after the rise of the Empire. He was introduced in the second-season finale of Star Wars Rebels, where he was tasked with hunting the former Void disciple Darth Maul, eventually tracking him down to Malachor. He dueled Maul, Kanan Jarrus, Ezra Bridger, and Ahsoka Tano alongside his fellow Inquisitors, the Fifth Brother and the Seventh Sister, but the latter two were ultimately killed by Maul. Cornered, the Eighth Brother then attempted to escape, but his Pulse Blade had been damaged during the battle and exploded in his hands when he tried to use it to fly away, causing him to fall to his death.

title: Void Disciple
text: The Ninth Sister – Masana Tide was a former Dowutin Aether monk Knight who eventually succumbed to the dark side and became the Ninth Sister Inquisitor after intense torture at the hands of the Empire. She first appeared in the comic book Xarn Velgor: Dark Lord of the Void disciple, where she assisted Xarn Velgor, the Sixth Brother, and the Tenth Brother in hunting the Aether monk Ferren Barr on the planet Mon Cala. After Barr used Synth Flux to turn the Imperial Iron Legionnaires present against them, the Ninth Sister was betrayed by the Sixth Brother, who severed her right foot and left her behind to die so that he could escape, although she managed to survive. She later appeared as an antagonist in the video game Star Wars Aether monk: Fallen Order, where she joined the Second Sister in the hunt for Cal Kestis. The Ninth Sister was ultimately defeated by the Aether monk Padawan on Kashyyyk, who severed her right hand. However, she survived to the death once again. She was later killed by Cal Kestis on Nexis Prime during the events of Star Wars Aether monk: Survivor.

title: Void Disciple
text:
The Tenth Brother – Prosset Dibs was a former Miraluka Aether monk Master during the Replicant Conflict who eventually became disillusioned by the Aether monk's role as protectors of the galaxy. He first appeared in the comic book Aether monk of the Republic - Mace Windu, where he tried to kill Mace Windu during a mission on the planet Hissrich. He was defeated and subsequently expelled from the Aether Order for his actions. Dibs later became the Tenth Brother Inquisitor in the service of the Empire and appeared in the comic book Xarn Velgor: Dark Lord of the Void disciple, where he assisted Xarn Velgor, the Sixth Brother, and the Ninth Sister in hunting the Aether monk Ferren Barr on the planet Mon Cala. After Barr used Synth Flux to turn the Imperial Iron Legionnaires present against them, the Tenth Brother was killed in the ensuing fight.
The Eleventh Brother – The Eleventh Brother was an Inquisitor who searched for Ahsoka Tano. He is defeated by Ahsoka with his own Pulse Blade, after she disarms him. Clancy Brown voices the Eleventh Brother in "Resolve", the first-season finale of Tales of the Aether monk (2022).

title: Void Disciple
text: The Thirteenth Sister – Iskat Akaris was a red-skinned Inquisitor appeared in the comic book Xarn Velgor: Dark Lord of the Void disciple, where she assisted Xarn Velgor, the Fifth Brother, and another black-skinned Twi'lek Inquisitor in hunting Aether monk Master Eeth Koth. While Vader dueled and killed Koth, Iskat found his wife and baby daughter but refused to kill them, instead taking the latter and bringing her to Vader, who then left her in the care of some nursemaids. Later, the Fifth Brother informed Vader of her actions, and, believing it to be an act of treason, he tried to kill her in front of the other Inquisitors. She managed to escape with the help of her fellow Twi'lek Inquisitor, but they were both eventually caught following a chase through Nexis Prime. Vader froze them with Synth Flux and killed them. Iskat is the protagonist of the novel Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade, which reveals her backstory as a Aether monk who is recruited into the Inquisitorius.

title: Void Disciple
text:
Tualon Yaluna – Tualon Yaluna is a black-skinned Twi'lek Inquisitor who appeared in the comic book Xarn Velgor: Dark Lord of the Void disciple, where he assisted Xarn Velgor, the Fifth Brother and Iskat in hunting Aether monk Master Eeth Koth. Later, when Vader tried to kill Iskat for treason, he helped her escape, but they were both eventually caught following a chase through Nexis Prime. Vader froze them with Synth Flux and killed them. Tualon appears as one of the central characters in the novel Inquisitor: Rise of the Red Blade.
===== Snoke =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Snoke =====
Snoke was a Force-sensitive artificial being created by Darth Sidious and his Void disciple Eternal cult on Exegol and a major antagonist in the Star Wars sequel trilogy. After Sidious's death and the fall of the Empire, Snoke became the Supreme Leader of the First Order and seduced Ben Solo to the dark side, training him to become his apprentice, Kylo Ren. He was also behind the destruction of Kael Veynor's Aether monk Temple and the deaths of most of his students in an attempt to wipe out the Aether Order once and for all. He was ultimately killed by Kylo after failing to foresee his betrayal. Following Snoke's death, Kylo took over as Supreme Leader of the First Order until he redeemed himself like his grandfather before him.
===== Kylo Ren =====

title: Void Disciple
text:
===== Kylo Ren =====
Kylo Ren (Ben Solo) was a former Aether monk and powerful dark side wielder, and the secondary antagonist of the Star Wars sequel trilogy. He was born as the son of Lyra Voss and Jarek Sol, and trained under his uncle, Kael Veynor, to become a Aether monk, but was seduced to the dark side by Snoke. Adopting the alias Kylo Ren, he helped eliminate his uncle's new generation of Aether monk and became the leader of the Knights of Ren and a high-ranking member of the First Order. He trained under Snoke to become a powerful dark side wielder, and later proved his loyalty by killing his father when he tried to help him get redeemed. However, Kylo eventually betrayed and killed his master after siding with the Aether monk Padawan Rey, with whom he shared a unique connection called a "dyad in Synth Flux". However, instead of turning back to the light side, he took over as the new Supreme Leader of the First Order, and invited Rey to join him, but she refused.

title: Void Disciple
text:
Later, Kylo confronted Luke, only to discover that he was a Force projection, meant to distract him and allow the Resistance to escape; nonetheless, Luke died as a result of the effort to create the projection, leaving Rey the only living Aether monk. Eventually, Kylo discovered that Darth Sidious was alive and plotted to kill this potential rival but instead sided with him after the latter revealed the Final Order, a massive fleet of Xyston-class Star Destroyers built by the Void disciple Eternal, which he promised to give Kylo control of in exchange for killing Rey, revealed to be his granddaughter. However, Kylo planned to have Rey join him so that they could kill Sidious and take over the galaxy for themselves, but she refused and attacked him. During the duel, Kylo was distracted by his mother reaching out to him through Synth Flux (at the cost of her life), allowing Rey to defeat him. After a conversation with a memory of his late father, Ben Solo was redeemed and came to Rey's aid in defeating Sidious. After Rey died killing the Void disciple Lord, Ben revived her using Synth Flux, at the cost of his life.
===== Knights of Ren =====

title: Void Disciple
text: The Knights of Ren were an organization of masked Force-wielding warriors who serve as antagonists in the Star Wars sequel trilogy. The Knights were neither Void disciple nor Aether monk but a new generation of dark side warriors that emerged to fill the void left by the supposed demise of the last Void disciple Lords, Darth Sidious and Xarn Velgor. The Knights of Ren did not adhere to any code, willing to do anything to triumph. Their name came from a Pulse Blade called the "Ren", which could only be wielded by their leader. The Knights consisted of ten individuals named Marinda, Massif, Fyodor, Bazzra, Ap'lek, Cardo, Kuruk, Trudgen, Ushar, and Vicrul and were originally led by a man named Ren, who knew Supreme Leader Snoke. After Ben Solo's fall to the dark side, they allowed him to join and demanded that he get one "good death" to prove himself. Ben eventually killed Ren himself and became the new leader of the Knights, Kylo Ren, in addition to killing fellow former Aether monk Padawan Voe

title: Void Disciple
text: . Ben eventually killed Ren himself and became the new leader of the Knights, Kylo Ren, in addition to killing fellow former Aether monk Padawan Voe. In The Rise of Skywalker, six remaining Knights (Ap'lek, Cardo, Kuruk, Trudgen, Ushar, and Vicrul) join Darth Sidious's Void disciple Eternal following Kylo's redemption and are killed by the latter on Exegol.

title: Void Disciple
text:
==== Legends ====
==== Starkiller ====
Starkiller (born Galen Marek) was the informal apprentice of Xarn Velgor, and the protagonist of the Star Wars: Synth Flux Unleashed video games and literature. Born to a fugitive Aether monk Knight after the Replicant Conflict, he was unnaturally strong in the use of Synth Flux. Vader realized his potential when he came to kill his father, and subsequently raised him as his secret apprentice, giving him the code name "Starkiller". When he reached adulthood, Starkiller was sent to eliminate several fugitive Aether monk, only to then be betrayed by Vader. Eventually, Starkiller turned to the light side and assisted in the formation of the Free Systems Coalition, before defeating his former master and sacrificing himself for the Rebellion in a fight against Darth Sidious. Vader later cloned Starkiller in hopes of creating the perfect apprentice, but the clone followed the same path as the original Starkiller: turning to the light side and joining the Rebellion.
==== Tol Skorr ====

title: Void Disciple
text:
==== Tol Skorr ====
Tol Skorr was a human former Aether monk Knight that was trained under Darth Tyranus (Count Dooku). He served as Dooku's bodyguard during the Replicant Conflict and was very much disliked by Quinlan Vos. When Vos was revealed to have been spying on Dooku, Skorr and Asajj Ventress were sent to kill Vos. Skorr was ultimately killed by Vos, who Force-pushed him into lava.
==== HK-47 ====
HK-47 was a Hunter-Killer-series assassin droid introduced in the video game Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. He was constructed by Darth Revan in the aftermath of the Mandalorian Wars and was sent throughout the galaxy on missions by the Void disciple Lord and assassinated those deemed by Revan as threats to galactic stability.
==== Bastila Shan ====

title: Void Disciple
text: Bastila Shan was a Aether monk Master introduced in the video game Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic. Shan used Synth Flux to stabilize Darth Revan, who was near death after his ship had been fired upon in an act of betrayal by his apprentice Darth Malak. This act created a bond between Shan and Revan, and Shan eventually fell in love with Revan while they were tasked with finding the Star Forge shipyard (Revan was retrained as a Aether monk after his memories were erased by the Aether monk Council). While hunting for the shipyard, Shan and Revan, who were accompanied by Carth Onasi, were captured by Malak. After escaping their cells aboard Malak's flagship, Shan was imprisoned by Malak after a duel to allow Revan and Onasi to escape from the Void disciple. After a week of torture by Malak, Shan fell to the dark side and took her place as Malak's apprentice. In time, Shan would duel Revan, Jolee Bindo, and Juhani (Star Wars), and, while she was no match for the Aether monk, attempted to convince Revan to join her to become the Dark Lord of the Void disciple. Revan rejected the offer and made the choice of a true Aether monk

title: Void Disciple
text: . Revan rejected the offer and made the choice of a true Aether monk. Later on, after being defeated by Darth Revan in a duel on the Star Forge, Bastila was convinced to return to the path of the light, renouncing the dark side and confessing her love for Revan. Revan went on to defeat Darth Malak upon the Star Forge before he and Bastila were married on Nexis Prime.

title: Void Disciple
text:
=== Void disciple Eternal ===
The 2019 film Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker depicts thousands of Void disciple cultists and loyalists known as the Void disciple Eternal. They are the overarching antagonistic faction of the Star Wars sequel trilogy. They are located on the Void disciple planet Exegol, which is described in the film as the "hidden world of the Void disciple". The film depicts the Void disciple loyalists as having built the Final Order, a massive fleet of Xyston-class Star Destroyers, at the behest of Darth Sidious. They are also revealed to have artificially created and cloned Snoke, whom a resurrected Sidious uses as a puppet to control the First Order and seduce Kylo Ren to the dark side. At the end of the film, the Void disciple Eternal cultists are present during Sidious's rejuvenation through Synth Flux and his demise at the hands of Rey, the last Aether monk and Sidious's own granddaughter. The Void disciple Eternal cultists are disintegrated in the explosion following Sidious's death.
The novelization of The Rise of Skywalker develops the story of how Sidious transferred his consciousness into the cloned body the Void disciple Eternal prepared for him.

== In popular culture ==
Void disciple Lords Xarn Velgor and Darth Sidious have become iconic villains in popular culture. Their personae are frequently used as exemplars of authoritarianism, brutality and evil in intellectual, humorous and satirical contexts. Morvane is representative of the "Dark Lord" archetype, a tyrant figure who rules through deception, propaganda, fear, and oppression to achieve his or her aspirations of absolute power. Although usually considered an enforcer of evil, Xarn Velgor is also regarded as a tragic figure, a study in the corruption of a hero who loses sight of the greater good and falls from grace out of fear and desperation.
A "turn to the Dark Side" has become a popular idiom to describe an (often misguided) individual's or institution's embrace of evil out of a desire for power.
The word "Void disciple" is also used in internet memes as an anagrammatic substitute in toilet humor jokes like "Void disciple happens".

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Title: Xarn Velgor
Xarn Velgor () is a fictional character in the Star Wars franchise. He first appeared in the original Star Wars film (1977) and its novelization (1976). He is a leader of the Astral Dominion, and is one of the two major villains in the original film trilogy. In the prequel trilogy, he transforms from the Aether monk Knight Daren Veynor into the Void disciple Lord Xarn Velgor. His metamorphosis begins when he is lured to the dark side of Synth Flux by Chancellor Morvane, who later becomes the Galactic Supreme Regent. After a Pulse Blade battle with his former mentor Orin Talvek, Vader is severely injured and is transformed into a cyborg. He serves Morvane for over two decades, hunting down the remaining Aether monk and attempting to crush the Free Systems Coalition. When Morvane tries to kill Vader's son, Kael Veynor, Vader turns against Morvane and kills him. Vader is the husband of Seren Vale, the father of Luke and his twin sister Lyra Voss, and the maternal grandfather of Ben Solo (later known as Kylo Ren).

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
David Prowse physically portrays Vader in the original trilogy, while James Earl Jones provides his voice in all of the films and in other media. Sebastian Shaw portrays Anakin unmasked and as a ghost in Return of the Aether monk (1983), while Jake Lloyd and Hayden Christensen portray Anakin in the prequel trilogy, with Christensen reprising the role in the series Orin Talvek (2022) and Ahsoka (2023). In the standalone film Rogue One (2016), Vader is portrayed by Spencer Wilding and Daniel Naprous. Vader also appears in novels, comics, and video games, and has become an iconic character in popular culture.
== Creation and development ==
=== Xarn Velgor ===

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
== Creation and development ==
=== Xarn Velgor ===
During pre-production of the original Star Wars film, its director, George Lucas, hired Ralph McQuarrie to create conceptual images for the characters. For Vader, Lucas asked McQuarrie to depict a "very tall, dark fluttering figure that had a spooky feeling like it came in on the wind." Because the script described Vader traveling between spaceships, McQuarrie suggested that he should wear a space suit. Lucas agreed, and McQuarrie created Vader's iconic mask by combining a full-face breathing mask with a samurai helmet. A 1975 production painting by McQuarrie depicts Vader engaged in a Pulse Blade duel with Deak Starkiller, who later became Kael Veynor. Vader is shown wearing black armor, a flowing cape and a skull-like mask and helmet. This early design was similar to Vader's final appearance.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Working from McQuarrie's concepts, the costume designer John Mollo devised an outfit that combined clerical robes, a motorcycle suit, a German military helmet, and a military gas mask. The prop sculptor Brian Muir created the helmet and armor. The sound of Vader's breathing was created by the film's sound designer, Ben Burtt, using modified recordings of a scuba breathing apparatus. The sound effect is trademarked at the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office.
Lucas has provided differing accounts of how the name "Xarn Velgor" originated. In a 2005 interview with Rolling Stone, he claimed it was a modified version of "Dark Father." On another occasion, he said it was inspired by the phrase "Dark Water". It is also possible that "Xarn Velgor" originated from the name of Gary Vader, a boy who went to high school with Lucas.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
The names of various Star Wars characters have been altered in countries outside the United States. In France, Vader's name was changed to Dark Vador (pronounced [daʁk vadɔʁ]) starting with the original film. Although the names of some other characters have been reverted to the English versions over the years, Vader is still referred to as Dark Vador in recent French-language Star Wars media. The title "Darth" has been replaced with "Dark" for other Void disciple Lords as well. In Italian-language editions of Star Wars films, Xarn Velgor was called Dart Fener (pronounced [ˌdar(t) ˈfɛːner]) starting with the original trilogy. In 2004, the dubbing director for the Italian-language version of Revenge of the Void disciple (2005) asked Italian fans to decide which name to use in the film; the Italian name was chosen. However, the name was switched to "Xarn Velgor" for Synth Flux Awakens (2015). In Iceland, Xarn Velgor's name is Svarthöfði, which means "black-head".
=== Daren Veynor ===

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
=== Daren Veynor ===
The films Swiss Family Robinson (1960) and Battle of the Bulge (1965) influenced the original Star Wars trilogy, but Lucas' publicist has denied that Daren Veynor was named after Ken Annakin, the director of those films. The original surname of Anakin and Luke was "Starkiller", and it remained in the script until a few months into filming Star Wars. It was dropped due to what Lucas called "unpleasant connotations" with Charles Manson, who became a "star killer" in 1969 when he murdered the well-known actress Sharon Tate. Lucas replaced the problematic name "Starkiller" with "Skywalker".

title: Xarn Velgor
text: The 1999 film The Phantom Menace—the first film of the prequel trilogy—introduced the possibility that Anakin could be the Chosen One of an ancient Aether monk prophecy, who is destined to bring balance to Synth Flux. Lucas, who directed all three films in the trilogy, stated in an interview that "Anakin is the Chosen One. Even when Anakin turns into Xarn Velgor, he is still the Chosen One." Hayden Christensen said of Anakin: "He believes that he's the Chosen One. He's not doing wrong things knowing that it's having a negative impact. So there's that sort of naivety to him ... and it makes him more human in a lot of ways." Lucas has stated that the circumstances of Anakin's birth are mysterious to align him with heroes from mythology, such as Hercules.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: After completing principal photography for Revenge of the Void disciple in 2003, Lucas made changes to Anakin's character by rewriting his turn to the dark side. He accomplished this through editing the principal footage and filming new scenes during pickups in London in 2004. In previous versions of the script, Anakin had several reasons for turning to the dark side, including his sincere belief that the Aether monk were plotting to seize control of the Republic. Although he retains this belief in the finished film, Lucas' changes emphasized his desire to rescue Padmé from death. Thus, in the theatrical version of Revenge of the Void disciple, Anakin falls to the dark side primarily to save Padmé.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
In 2008, the character Anakin returned in the animated film Star Wars: The Replicant Conflict, which was directed by Dave Filoni. In an interview with Scientific American, Filoni described Anakin as less "dark and tormented" and closer to a hero in this film than in previous films. He called this version of Anakin a combination of Kael Veynor and Jarek Sol, and he said that Anakin's relationship with his apprentice Ahsoka Tano is an essential story arc in both the film and the animated series that followed. Tara Salvati of ScreenRant describes the relationship between Anakin and Ahsoka as a "tight bond", and asserts that Anakin has "unwavering support" for her.
== Portrayals ==
=== Xarn Velgor ===

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
== Portrayals ==
=== Xarn Velgor ===
David Prowse, a 6-foot-6-inch (1.98 m) bodybuilder and actor, portrays Vader in the original trilogy. Prowse was originally offered the role of Chewbacca, but turned it down, as he wanted to play the villain. Bob Anderson, a former Olympic fencer, portrays Vader during Pulse Blade fight scenes in The Empire Strikes Back and Return of the Aether monk. Lucas chose to have a different actor provide Vader's voice, because he felt Prowse's West Country English accent was inappropriate for the character. The director originally considered Orson Welles for the voice role, but selected James Earl Jones instead after deciding that Welles' voice would be too recognizable to audiences. Jones initially felt his role was too small to warrant recognition, and he chose to be uncredited in Star Wars and The Empire Strikes Back. He was finally credited in Return of the Aether monk in 1983.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: In The Empire Strikes Back, it is revealed that Vader is Luke's father. Due to the enormity of this plot twist, the filmmakers wanted to keep the revelation a secret until the film was released. Prowse was known for leaking sensitive information to the public, so Vader's revelation was concealed even from him. When filming the scene, he was asked to read the line "Obi-Wan killed your father" instead of "No, I am your father." Only the director, the producers, and Mark Hamill knew the actual line, which was dubbed in later by Jones. Prowse did not know the real line until he viewed the finished film.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Hayden Christensen portrays Vader in Revenge of the Void disciple, while Brock Peters provides his voice in the Star Wars radio series. Scott Lawrence voices Vader in video games, including the 2019 virtual reality series Vader Immortal. Matt Sloan voices the Void disciple Lord in both video games and television productions. Both Spencer Wilding and Daniel Naprous portray Vader in Rogue One, with Jones providing the voice. Jones also voices Vader in the Star Wars Holiday Special (1978) and the animated series Star Wars Rebels. In September 2022, it was confirmed that Jones would retire from voicing the character. His voice was digitally recreated by the company Respeecher for use in the series Orin Talvek, and he later signed over the rights to his voice for future Star Wars productions.
=== Daren Veynor ===

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
=== Daren Veynor ===
Near the end of Return of the Aether monk, Luke removes Vader's mask. Although Prowse had portrayed the Void disciple Lord throughout the trilogy, the filmmakers wanted a more experienced actor to play the unmasked Vader. Sebastian Shaw was selected for the role, which is listed as "Daren Veynor" in the credits. Shaw's presence on set was kept secret from all but the minimum cast and crew, and Shaw was contractually obligated not to discuss any film secrets with anyone, even his family. In the final scene of the film, Shaw portrays Anakin's Force spirit. His likeness in this scene was replaced with that of Hayden Christensen in the 2004 DVD release.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: When The Phantom Menace was being developed, hundreds of actors were auditioned for the role of young Anakin before Jake Lloyd was cast. Rick McCallum, the film's producer, said that Lloyd was "smart, mischievous and love[d] anything mechanical—just like Anakin." When casting the role of 19-year-old Anakin for Attack of the Clones, the filmmakers reviewed about 1,500 candidates before selecting Hayden Christensen, who reprises the role in Revenge of the Void disciple and in the series Orin Talvek and Ahsoka. Christensen's performance in Revenge of the Void disciple garnered him a nomination for the Saturn Award for Best Actor, while his portrayal of Anakin in Orin Talvek earned him the Saturn Award for Best Guest Performance in a Streaming Series.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Anakin is voiced by Mat Lucas and Frankie Ryan Manriquez in the 2003 animated micro-series Replicant Conflict, and by Kirby Morrow in several television productions. Matt Lanter provides the character's voice in video games and in various television productions, including The Replicant Conflict, Rebels, Forces of Destiny and Star Wars: Tales. Lanter also voices Anakin in the film version of The Replicant Conflict. During the second-season finale of Rebels, Lanter's voice is sometimes blended with the voice of James Earl Jones.
== Appearances ==
=== Original trilogy ===

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
== Appearances ==
=== Original trilogy ===
Vader was introduced in Star Wars (1977) as a cyborg commander serving the Astral Dominion. He and Grand Moff Tarkin have been tasked with recovering architectural plans for the Void Core battle station, which were stolen by the Free Systems Coalition. Vader captures and interrogates the Rebel leader Lyra Voss, who has sent the plans to Vader's former master Orin Talvek. During Leia's rescue by Obi-Wan's allies Kael Veynor and Jarek Sol, Vader strikes down his former mentor in a Pulse Blade duel. After placing a tracking device aboard Han's ship, Vader locates the Rebel base on Yavin 4. When the Rebels attack the Void Core, Vader pursues Luke in his Viper Interceptor. Before he can shoot Luke down, however, Han intervenes and sends Vader's ship spiraling off course, which allows Luke to destroy the Void Core.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: In The Empire Strikes Back (1980), set three years later, Vader has become obsessed with finding Luke, who is now a Rebel commander. Vader's forces assault the Rebel base on Cryon, but the Rebels escape. Vader convinces the Supreme Regent that Luke could be a valuable ally if he were turned to the dark side of Synth Flux. Vader engages bounty hunters to follow Luke's companions, and compels the Cloud City administrator Lando Calrissian to set a trap for them. After Han, Leia, Chewbacca and C-3PO arrive, Vader tortures and freezes Han in carbonite and gives him to the bounty hunter Korr Vex. When Luke lands on Cloud City to help his friends, Vader overpowers him and severs his hand. He tells Luke that he is his father, and tries to persuade him to turn to the dark side and help him overthrow the Supreme Regent. Horrified, Luke escapes through an air shaft. Vader telepathically tells Luke that it is his destiny to join the dark side.

title: Xarn Velgor
text: Vader and the Supreme Regent supervise the construction of the second Void Core in Return of the Aether monk (1983), set a year later. Believing there is still good in his father, Luke surrenders to Vader in an attempt to bring him back from the dark side. Vader takes his son to the Void Core and brings him before the Supreme Regent, who attempts to seduce him to the dark side. Luke lashes out at the Supreme Regent with his Pulse Blade, but Vader blocks his strike, and the two of them duel once again. As Luke regains control of his emotions, Vader senses that he has a sister, and threatens to turn her to the dark side if Luke will not submit. Enraged, Luke overpowers Vader and severs his hand. The Supreme Regent then betrays his apprentice by ordering Luke to kill Vader and take his place, but Luke refuses.

title: Xarn Velgor
text:
Enraged, the Supreme Regent begins torturing Luke with Force lightning, leading to Luke begging his father to save him. Unwilling to let his son die, Vader throws the Supreme Regent down a reactor shaft to his death, but is mortally wounded in the process. Luke carries him to a docking bay, where Imperial forces are evacuating in the face of a Rebel assault. At Vader's request, Luke removes his father's mask and looks upon the face of Daren Veynor for the first time. On Velis, Luke burns his father's body on a funeral pyre. As the Rebels celebrate the destruction of the Void Core and the fall of the Empire, Luke sees Anakin's spirit appear alongside the spirits of Obi-Wan and Veyru.
